💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, everton Under-21s secured their first point in the Premier League International Cup with a 1-1 draw against Borussia Mönchengladbach at Walton Hall Park.
  • Everton Under-21s secured their first point in the Premier League International Cup with a 1-1 draw against Borussia Mönchengladbach at Walton Hall Park.
  • Both goals came in the first half, with Scottish youth international striker Ceiran Loney’s close-range effort cancelling out an early opener from Josiah Uwakhonye.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, everton Under-21s secured their first point in the Premier League International Cup with a 1-1 draw against Borussia Mönchengladbach at Walton Hall Park. Both goals came in the first half, with Scottish youth international striker Ceiran Loney’s close-range effort cancelling out an early opener from Josiah Uwakhonye. The only change from the Under-21s’ comeback victory over Middlesbrough the previous Friday saw Shea Pita start on the right wing ahead of Jonathan Nsangou, with Harvey Foster returning to the squad and Under-18s midfielder Freddie Murdock named on the substitutes’ bench. The first chance of the game fell to the Toffees in the fifth minute, and it was close to breaking the deadlock. Midfielder Melvin Matos received a square ball on the edge of the box from Braiden Graham but his side-footed effort flew narrowly wide of Marcello Trippel’s right-hand post. Toffees goalkeeper George Pickford had to be alert to make a smart save with his feet two minutes later as Finnish midfielder Taavi Koukkumäki shifted in the box away from centre-back Luis Gardner and found space for a shot.But Mönchengladbach would take the lead moments later. Captain Nico Vidic, on the turn, played a stunning through ball that split midfield and defence to find Uwakhonye, who was onside and duly slotted past Pickford for 1-0. Uwakhonye thought he had secured his second in the 17th minute, only for a combination of Gardner and centre-back partner John Dodds to get enough on the ball to deflect it wide. Slowly but surely however the Toffees wrestled back the initiative from the visitors and started to cause problems through Pita, Graham, Loney and Malik Olayiwola. Very soon, the hosts were on top. By the 35th minute, Everton had a deserved equaliser through a striker’s finish from Loney. Right-back George Finney and Graham combined nicely on the right, with the latter finding Pita in an advanced position on the wing. Pita beat his man for pace before clipping a cross to the penalty spot, which Graham flicked on to the back post. Loney wrestled with his marker but got his leg to the ball first, turning it home for his first goal of the season.Loney thought he had his second minutes later when Pita sent a low ball across the box, but it was just in front of the Toffees’ striker’s outstretched boot. It could have been 2-1 in added time when Olayiwola, taking the ball on half-way, set off at goal. His dribble to the edge of the box was excellent, leaving one defender trailing in his wake, and his shot looked destined for the top-right corner, only for Trippel to tip the ball onto his near post and breathe a sigh of relief as he watched it roll across the goal-line and away from danger. The second half began in the same manner as the first, with the Toffees on top but unable to turn their chances into goals, and the game became testy as a series of strong challenges flew in, with eight bookings dished out by referee Zac Kennard-Kettle by the game’s conclusion, six of which were shown to the opposition. Everton Under-21s secured their first point in the Premier League International Cup with a 1-1 draw against Borussia Mönchengladbach at Walton Hall Park.

Both goals came in the first half, with Scottish youth international striker Ceiran Loney’s close-range effort cancelling out an early opener from Josiah Uwakhonye.

The only change from the Under-21s’ comeback victory over Middlesbrough the previous Friday saw Shea Pita start on the right wing ahead of Jonathan Nsangou, with Harvey Foster returning to the squad and Under-18s midfielder Freddie Murdock named on the substitutes’ bench.

The first chance of the game fell to the Toffees in the fifth minute, and it was close to breaking the deadlock. Midfielder Melvin Matos received a square ball on the edge of the box from Braiden Graham but his side-footed effort flew narrowly wide of Marcello Trippel’s right-hand post.

Toffees goalkeeper George Pickford had to be alert to make a smart save with his feet two minutes later as Finnish midfielder Taavi Koukkumäki shifted in the box away from centre-back Luis Gardner and found space for a shot.

But Mönchengladbach would take the lead moments later. Captain Nico Vidic, on the turn, played a stunning through ball that split midfield and defence to find Uwakhonye, who was onside and duly slotted past Pickford for 1-0.

Uwakhonye thought he had secured his second in the 17th minute, only for a combination of Gardner and centre-back partner John Dodds to get enough on the ball to deflect it wide.

Sources indicate that slowly but surely however the Toffees wrestled back the initiative from the visitors and started to cause problems through Pita, Graham, Loney and Malik Olayiwola. Very soon, the hosts were on top.

By the 35th minute, Everton had a deserved equaliser through a striker’s finish from Loney. Right-back George Finney and Graham combined nicely on the right, with the latter finding Pita in an advanced position on the wing.

Sources indicate that pita beat his man for pace before clipping a cross to the penalty spot, which Graham flicked on to the back post. Loney wrestled with his marker but got his leg to the ball first, turning it home for his first goal of the season.

Loney thought he had his second minutes later when Pita sent a low ball across the box, but it was just in front of the Toffees’ striker’s outstretched boot.

It has been revealed that it could have been 2-1 in added time when Olayiwola, taking the ball on half-way, set off at goal. His dribble to the edge of the box was excellent, leaving one defender trailing in his wake, and his shot looked destined for the top-right corner, only for Trippel to tip the ball onto his near post and breathe a sigh of relief as he watched it roll across the goal-line and away from danger.

The second half began in the same manner as the first, with the Toffees on top but unable to turn their chances into goals, and the game became testy as a series of strong challenges flew in, with eight bookings dished out by referee Zac Kennard-Kettle by the game’s conclusion, six of which were shown to the opposition.

Justin Clarke attempted to force an opening late on after being introduced for Pita, one particularly promising run seeing him battle past three defenders in the box, only for his cross-come-shot to fly wide of the far post.

Tech Report: What are fossil fuels?

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life.
  • The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.
  • They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that whether in the form of crumbly rock, odorless gas or slick black liquid, ancient organic compounds have powered the flourishing of modern life. But now they threaten to make the planet unlivable for many plants, animals and humans.

The collective term refers to coal, oil and natural gas — a group of energy sources that contain carbon and hydrogen.

They started life hundreds of millions of years ago as living plants and animals. When they died, they sank to the bottom of oceans and swamps where they decomposed under layers of sediment.

Over time, this matter was buried deeper and deeper into the earth, subjecting it to increasing pressure and heat which changed its chemical composition. Plants and trees transformed into coal, whereas microscopic plankton and algae became oil and — if the heat and pressure increased further — gas.

Today fossil fuels can be found in the earth's crust all around the world although some countries, such as the US, Saudi Arabia and Russia, have bigger reserves than others.

Coal, found in underground coal beds, is extracted by mining, whereas oil and gas, found in reservoirs beneath the land and ocean, are accessed by drilling.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Since the early 19th Century, when the discovery and exploitation of fossil fuel reserves powered the Industrial Revolution, our use of them has skyrocketed, increasing eight-fold since 1950.

Today they provide 80% of our energy needs through heating, electricity generation and transport.

We transform them into energy either by burning them directly in furnaces that warm up our homes and businesses, or in power plants to heat water into steam which then generates electricity. When it comes to transport, crude oil is refined into a range of products such as diesel, gasoline and kerosene that are burned in the engines of automobiles, airplanes and ships. Natural gas is also sometimes compressed for use in cars and buses.

But fossil fuels are also essential to a huge range of products including steel, formed using a coal-derived material called coke, and plastic, which is produced by refining and processing crude oil and gas.

Fossil fuels are by far the biggest contributors to climate change. When burned to power our modern lives, they emit carbon dioxide (CO2) into Earth's atmosphere, trapping heat and causing temperatures to rise.

It has been revealed that with 2025 officially one of the warmest years on record, the impact of these emissions is being felt around the world. Hotter temperatures are causing polar ice caps to melt and creating the conditions for extreme weather events — such as floods, drought, wildfires and storms — to become more intense and frequent.

Recent findings suggest that scientists stress the need to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) to avoid unleashing the most catastrophic impacts of climate change. That was laid out in the 2015 Paris Agreement. Currently, there are 194 parties to the agreement, but progress has been too slow, and overall emissions continue to rise.

Sources indicate that three years after countries agreed at the UN climate conference in Dubai COP28 to transition away from coal, oil and gas. After the previous COP in Brazil failed to reach a consensus on a concrete strategy, Brazil has now presented a roadmap aimed at turning that promise into national plans.

"It is long past time to stop treating the transition away from fossil fuels as taboo or intractable," United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated.

Hill Dickinson Stadium will be transformed into a festive destination this December as Everton unveils The Magic of Christmas – a packed programme of family experiences, Christmas parties, festive dining and entertainment at the Club’s waterfront home.

For the first time, the stadium will host a dedicated programme of Christmas events, giving Evertonians, families, friends, businesses and visitors to the city the chance to experience Hill Dickinson Stadium in a completely different way.

Running throughout December, The Magic of Christmas will feature the spectacular new Enchanted Lights experience, the return of Breakfast with Santa, two Après-Ski Christmas Party Nights and a special Christmas Bottomless Brunch at Domingo’s Bar & Grill.

Whether it’s a magical family day out, a Christmas celebration with friends or an end-of-year party with colleagues, there will be something for everyone at Hill Dickinson Stadium this festive season.

Supporters and visitors can explore the full programme and book their Christmas experience at hilldickinsonstadium.com/christmas.

ENCHANTED LIGHTS.

Friday 11 December - Wednesday 23 December.

At the heart of The Magic of Christmas will be Enchanted Lights, a brand-fresh family experience bringing Hill Dickinson Stadium to life with light, music and festive entertainment.

Guests will begin their Christmas journey on Everton Way before entering an illuminated trail filled with festive installations and photo opportunities.

From there, visitors will enjoy a unique opportunity to enter Hill Dickinson Stadium through the West Stand Players’ Entrance, following the same route used by Jordan Pickford, Jack Grealish, James Tarkowski and Everton’s First Team on matchdays.

The journey continues down the Players’ Tunnel and out into the stadium, where guests will take their seats pitchside for a dazzling Christmas light show inside Everton’s waterfront home.

The experience then continues at Christmas in The Yard, a specially-created festive village offering seasonal food and drink alongside live entertainment.

Families can make their visit even more memorable by adding a trip to Santa’s Grotto, giving younger visitors the opportunity to meet Father Christmas.

Guests booking by Sunday 1 November can take advantage of an Early Bird offer of 20%% off adult and junior tickets by using the code HDSLIGHTS at checkout.

Families can also add a visit to Santa’s Grotto for £10 per child, available for juniors and infants.

Guests with a valid event ticket will also benefit from free parking at Nelson Dock, while flexible booking allows visitors to move their booking up to 36 hours before their selected time.

*Free infant tickets do not include entry to Santa’s Grotto unless the optional Grotto experience is purchased.

[CLICK HERE TO BOOK ENCHANTED LIGHTS].

BREAKFAST WITH SANTA.

Friday 18 December - Wednesday 23 December.

Father Christmas will also return to Hill Dickinson Stadium for the Club’s popular Breakfast with Santa experience.

Families can enjoy a festive breakfast and Christmas activities before meeting Santa himself, with every child receiving a special gift from Santa to take home.

The experience also includes an exclusive mini stadium tour, taking guests behind the scenes at Hill Dickinson Stadium, through the Players’ Tunnel and pitchside for a special festive photo opportunity.

Tickets are priced at:.

Breakfast with Santa is expected to be extremely popular and places are limited, so families are encouraged to book early to avoid missing out.

APRÈS-SKI CHRISTMAS PARTY NIGHTS.

Friday 11 December and Saturday 12 December.

Trade the slopes for the stadium as Hill Dickinson Stadium transforms into an alpine-inspired party destination for two special Après-Ski Christmas Party Nights.

Guests can enjoy festive food and drinks alongside a live singer, DJ, saxophone and bongo performers, themed dancers and immersive alpine-style entertainment throughout the evening.

Tickets include two festive food vouchers and two drinks vouchers, making either night an ideal option for Christmas parties or celebrations with friends, family or colleagues.

Private Christmas party packages are also available for groups looking for their own exclusive festive celebration.

Domingo’s Bar & Grill will also receive a festive makeover for a special Christmas Bottomless Brunch.

Priced at £85 per person, the experience includes 90 minutes of bottomless drinks, a specially-created festive brunch menu and music from a live DJ.

Guests can choose from mimosa, beer, wine or prosecco, while the menu includes festive sliders, loaded sausage rolls, Christmas dinner bowls, loaded mac and cheese and a selection of Santa’s sweets.

For an additional £10 per person, guests can upgrade to an unlimited premium cocktail package.

RANGERS 3 ABERDEEN 2: Amid all the thrills and spills, McInnes' triple switch sparks second-half revival

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 18:40 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:50 EST, 24 November 2026.

When these sides last met in the league at the end of August, Rangers were in such a dark place that you wondered if their season was already destined to be another thoroughly miserable episode.

Coming just three days after going out of Europe — for the second time — to an ordinary Jablonec team, the slender win Derek McInnes’ side claimed at Pittodrie that day felt like a can being kicked down the road.

Recent findings suggest that in those early weeks, the players looked lost. The manager admitted that he didn’t know what style of football he was watching. The supporters were preparing for a long, hard winter.

Recent findings suggest that it’s remarkable what can come from one scruffy win on the road. From that point to this, McInnes’ men have now gone 14 games unbeaten in all competitions.

Industry observers note that they have the League Cup final to look forward to next month. They are now just one point behind Celtic in the Premiership and look eminently capable of putting in a serious challenge for the title. In keeping with so many performances throughout this run, however, this wasn’t particularly convincing. Flat and rudderless for 45 minutes, Rangers were deservedly a goal behind at the interval.

In a recent development, credit where it’s due, though. Their response at the outset of the second period was outstanding with three goals coming in 11 minutes courtesy of Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin.

That ought to have been the platform for many more to follow. But the performance slipped back a level. Aberdeen scored once and could easily have scored again.

Raskin (right) and Gassama celebrate after combining to put Rangers 3-1 up.

Naderi capitalises on Muller's mishandling to fire Rangers level at the start of the second half.

According to recent reports, it was a truly thrilling match, full of slip-ups, incidents and moments of brilliance. The final stages were a tough watch for the home fans who hoped against hope that they’d see their side ease towards a routine victory.

Industry observers note that as at Fir Park on Saturday, though, Rangers found a way and added another win to the ledger. And provided that remains the case in the coming weeks and months, none of the light blue legions will be complaining.

Despite ultimately not having quite enough to take something, Aberdeen manager Mario Frick will have been encouraged by much of what he saw here.

Had it not been for that atrocious spell at the outset of the second period, he’d have fancied his men to take something.

They certainly fashioned plenty of opportunities. It was the defensive side of the game which ultimately cost them.

Recent findings suggest that mcInnes drafted in Kevin Kelsy, James Penrice and Ben Godfrey with Dujon Sterling, Tuur Rommens and Kim Minsu dropping out. There was a change of shape too, with a switch to a 3-5-2. For the longest time, it did not work.

Lyons gets his head to Marshall's corner to put Aberdeen in front in the first half.

While Frick kept faith with the diamond-shaped midfield which served him so well in Ayrshire, he made three changes. In came Ayoub Mouloua, Afeez Aremu and Findlay Marshall at the expense of Hicham Mahou, Ante Palaversa and Stuart Armstrong.

Before the game, there was a minute’s silence in memory of the late, great Ralph Brand. What a pity a couple of clowns in the visiting section were unable to keep their mouths shut for that long.

Rangers started brightly with Penrice’s delivery from the left causing chaos. Dan Neil had a stab at it, then Naderi. Aberdeen survived.

Once Frick’s side settled, Nicky Devlin’s cross was met by Marshall. His header was straight at Ivor Pandur.

Rangers’ general play was broken, their build-up more ponderous than patient. Gassama did manage to drop a shoulder and get a strike away but Aremu’s positioning ensured Marius Muller was untroubled.

According to recent reports, naderi was again Rangers’ most effective player, although the bar was set pretty low initially. The Czech’s lay-off invited Godfrey to let fly. His strike was well off target.

According to recent reports, while Gassama got into plenty of promising positions, his crossing continually let him down early on. On the other flank, Badredine Bouanani could not do right for doing wrong.

Sources indicate that when the ball broke kindly to Naderi on the edge of the box, Ibrox expected the net to bulge. This time the man of the moment fired over. Rangers’ efforts in the first half were summed up by Naderi being tripped by Gavin Molloy on the edge of the box. Bouanani’s effort from the free-kick was woeful.

According to recent reports, aberdeen were aggressive and organised. And when the moment arose, they went forward in numbers.

McInnes indicates his delight after his half-time changes helped turn the game around.

They edged in front on the half hour after Marshall won a corner which was a consequence of Frick’s men being prepared to back themselves.

Recent findings suggest that marshall curled the set-piece deep to the far post. Brad Lyons seemed to be invisible to those in light blue as he made a late run. Olwethu Makhanya belatedly reacted but it was too late.

Lyons got enough on his header to beat Pandur and force Raskin to make the block behind his keeper.

The minute the scoreboard indicated that VAR were checking for a goal, you suspected the Belgian hadn’t done quite enough to keep it out. After a lengthy delay came confirmation of that fact.

How would Rangers respond up until the break? Not terribly well. Lyons’ crude foul on Gassama gave Bouanani a chance to make amends with a set-piece. This one smashed into the wall. Seconds later, the winger fired well over the top when he ought to have done better.

In a recent development, the Dons could easily have doubled their advantage. Jack Milne carried well and rattled the ball into Kevin Nisbet’s feet. The forward played a smart pass around the corner. Mouloua was only denied by a terrific save from Pandur.

There was still time for Mouloua to be thwarted by the outstretched leg of Makhanya as he moved to turn home a cut back.

Sources indicate that bluntly, it was no surprise that McInnes made three changes at the break. Off came Godfrey, Kelsy and Bouanani. On went Minsu, Rommens and Findlay Curtis. The impact was extraordinary.

In a recent development, re-energised, within 45 seconds Rangers were level. Minsu’s speculative shot did come through heavy traffic. Still, Muller had to hold it. Credit to Naderi for anticipating the fumble. The instant it bounced towards him, he instinctively lashed it home for his 10th of the season. Subdued to that point, the home fans roared their approval. And they’d quickly be off their seats again.

According to recent reports, as Aberdeen’s attack broke down, Naderi played a simple pass into space. Gassama had too much pace for the chasing pack. Did he have the finishing? Absolutely. What a turnaround.

Gassama squeezes his shot under Muller to put the home side ahead just after the restart.

Industry observers note that two goals in 90 seconds then became three in 11 second-half minutes. Gassama did superbly to motor down the left, look up and play in Raskin. The Belgian smashed the ball back across goal and in.

That should have been that. Yet three minutes later, the Dons were back within a goal of McInnes’ men. Afforded too much time on the left, Alexander Briedl picked out Marshall with his cross. Marshall swept it home with his left foot via the inside of the post.

Remarkably, the Dons might well have levelled. Pandur made a fine save when Minsu threatened to turn an Aberdeen corner into his own net. The ball bounced off Nisbet and just wide.

Terrific throughout, Marshall saw a good strike whistle just wide. The fact the Dons made Rangers sweat for the win will be some consolation.

Breaking: Jensen Huang: Spy row, affairs leave Nvidia without its rockstar CEO

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.
  • In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.
  • The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide on CEO Jensen Huang's future as reports emerged of other extramarital affairs — this time with employees.

In a statement issued on Thursday, the world's most valuable chip supplier said Huang was resigning as President, CEO and board member, effective immediately.

The firm added that current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Colette Kress would become interim CEO.

Under Nvidia's bylaws, Huang can be removed "with or without cause" by a majority vote of its 11 directors.

The Upcoming York Times first reported that the 63-year-old Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him.

Later Thursday, Reuters news agency alleged an intimate relationship between Huang and a second employee, citing unidentified sources.

It has been revealed that those revelations emerged just three days after Huang admitted a relationship with a Chinese woman, whom United States intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The woman, Alice Huang — no relation — is a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that runs artificial intelligence (AI) data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia.

The US government is investigating the startup on suspicion that it secretly sent some of its Nvidia chips to China, violating Washington's curbs on high-end semiconductors.

Those advanced Nvidia processors ‌are ​used to train and run the large AI models behind chatbots and other generative AI products.

According to recent reports, megaspeed denies the allegations and on Thursday pledged to cooperate with US investigators. Huang, the alleged spy, has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan — a key chipmaking island.

While Nvidia's board backed its CEO after the first scandal emerged, market watchers believe the second caused too much reputational damage to one of the world's top three companies by market value.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang doesn't believe in formal succession planning, so with little notice, Nvidia appointed CFO Kress as interim CEO.

Bloomberg reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is working with advisers to identify potential permanent successors.

Kress, other senior Nvidia executives and members of Huang's own family have been mooted as replacements. The family members include his daughter Madison, a senior director of product marketing, and his son Spencer, who right now works in the firm's robotics division.

It has been revealed that rumors also abound over a longer-term solution. On India's CNBC-TV18, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld from the Yale School of Management floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook and ex-Google CEO Eric Schmidt.

US President Donald Trump also backed Cook on social media, writing: "A Legend replaces a Legend.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The scandals have certainly hit Nvidia's market value. Since the first extramarital affair emerged on Sunday, the chipmaker's market capitalization has fallen by well over $600 billion to $4.2 trillion.

Sources indicate that nvidia shares were down more than 9% in premarket trading Thursday, after dropping by 10% earlier this week. Some analysts expect the stock price to struggle in the short term.

Nvidia stock hit all-time highs just a month ago as US technology giants continued to announce billions in spending on AI infrastructure.

Demand for Nvidia's advanced chips is so high, however, that many market analysts expect little impact on near-term sales.

"While Jensen [Huang] is the heart and lungs of the Nvidia story…the tech giant and its leading-edge GPU technology will go on and [his departure] does not change the entrenched position Nvidia has in the AI Revolution chip arms race," mentioned Dan Ives, a partner, senior managing director and tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, a US-based merchant bank.

In a recent development, analysts see the biggest long-term risk in strategy and execution. After all, Huang was the leader who picked which ideas Nvidia should bet heavily on and got the whole organization behind them.

His sudden exit is also seen as highly disruptive to the chip designer's strong relationships with AI hyperscalers, Taiwanese chip producer TSMC and foreign governments — especially China.

Huang was Nvidia's main lobbyist on US chip export rules and persuaded US President Donald Trump to ease some curbs on China last year.

Huang is often called a rockstar CEO for his leather jackets instead of suits.

Like Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, he was also seen as a key-person risk as Nvidia’s public image, strategic direction and technical decisions became closely tied to him.

Huang steered the company for more than three decades and was also respected for his hands-on involvement in product architecture and engineering decisions.

He also insisted on a flat management structure, with around 60 executives reporting directly to him.

Huang has run the firm so tightly around his own technical judgment and product decisions that investors may have little sense of how it would function without him.

Sources indicate that at the same time, Nvidia is no longer the startup Huang founded in 1993. The company has built deep expertise in chip design and software, creating a durable moat that helps protect its huge profits, which topped $120.1 billion last year.

Some analysts argue that its central role in the AI hardware buildout makes it less dependent on Huang’s day-to-day input.

China is quickly playing catch-up with the US in the global race for AI dominance.

While Chinese AI models have lagged behind the likes of ChatGPT and Claude, recent updates from DeepSeek, Alibaba and Moonshot have closed much of the gap on benchmark tests and often beat US rivals on cost and speed.

Beijing is also investing heavily in domestic chips and data centers to reduce reliance on US hardware.

The US has curbed exports to China of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips.

However, this move has only slowed the pace of China's AI ambitions.

Reuters reported Thursday that Chinese AI firms are now trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity at data centers outside China, amid fears the US could further tighten restrictions on advanced chips.

Also Thursday, Beijing accused the US of using the Nvidia spying claims as a pretext to impose a technological "blockade" on China.

The glitch is likely to dominate talks next week between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen in southern China.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce.
  • The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

In a recent development, “I have to take the responsibility,” he noted. “We did not transfer the things we did in training. Hitting long balls all the time, that was not the initiative. We were not brave enough to play short passes.

In a recent development, “As soon as the referee blew his whistle, the initiative disappeared. We could feel the anger and the frustration, I felt it on the touchline. We are low on confidence and it reveals.”.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle looked listless, clueless and alarmingly devoid of belief in what they were being asked to do. They have the unmistakable whiff of a team in decline.

In a recent development, if they do not start playing a lot better, they will be worried about a relegation battle. It is four defeats in their last five games and the confidence in Jaissle to find solutions is fading. Rather than change what he is asking his team to do, he has doubled down on the formation and tactics.

Concerns have been creeping steadily upwards since August. There is a lack of confidence in the players, and worries about the quality of the eight fresh signings made over the summer.

In particular, there are serious misgivings about the implementation of the “vertical football” Jaissle has imported to the North East of England from the Austro-German Red Bull coaching school.

A night under the lights at St James’ Park should be a boisterous affair, but things went flat quickly. Newcastle, as they have tended to do this season, resorted to long balls punted forward. More often than not they were poorly directed – only 22 per cent were accurate over 98 minutes.

Industry observers note that there was no fluency and no threat. The first groans were heard inside 15 minutes as another pass was hoisted harmlessly into the air. They grew more widespread and more frequent.

Everton, just as they had in their Carabao Cup win last week, looked comfortable. Recognising how easy it was to nullify Newcastle’s game initiative, they offered an attacking threat of their own.

Industry observers note that A rising shot from Merlin Röhl briefly had goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek worried. A free-kick into the Newcastle box caused panic. James Tarkowski won the first header, but Thierno Barry swung and missed with his left foot.

The groans began to turn into boos and whistles. Jaissle’s side could barely string more than two passes together. It felt precarious.

According to recent reports, this is not an easy place to play football when the crowd airs its displeasure. As the first half limped on, there were players in black and white who looked like they could not handle the pressure.

It was a horrible game of football. With the last kick of the half, Everton should have taken the lead, Harrison Armstrong picked out Barry inside the box, but he made a mess of the finish. The referee’s whistle was accompanied by boos and a scream of “sort it out” from behind Jaissle’s technical area.

Sources indicate that he did not follow those blunt instructions. Everton took the lead in such simple fashion and all Jaissle and his coaching staff could do was shake their heads at each other. Tyrique George was played in far too easily from a free-kick but his shot should have been saved by Hornicek. It was straight at the Czech, but it went through him and it left Barry with a tap in. Newcastle appealed for both a foul on Fabian Schar and an offside but got neither.

It has been revealed that everton had the lead and it was so easy and straightforward. They waited for Newcastle to give the ball away and then broke at speed. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was superb and forced a fingertip save from Hornicek. From the resulting corner, Hornicek was needed again to keep out Jake O’Brien’s header.

Newcastle tried to gain some momentum and finally created a chance. Harvey Barnes curled a cross to the far post. It bounced awkwardly but Anthony Elanga somehow failed to bundle it across the line.

Jacob Ramsey sees red after coming on as a second-half substitute 🟥 https://t.co/26t7GkRdcg.

Recent findings suggest that “Lots of the game it was [one of their best performances]. We probably had better chances in the first half. [Not taking them] kept it really difficult. Getting the first goal was notable. Incredibly proud of the team all the time because their effort is unquestionable. There is not a lot of them but they are doing a great job and hope it continues.

It has been revealed that “We are creating chances, that is the significant thing for me. Thierno [Barry] has had some big opportunities. He was on the spot today. I was worried ‘was he on or offside at the time?’. I do not think anyone enjoys playing the same team twice so rapidly. So for us to win both is hugely notable for us. We want to get back to the top end of the league, it is incredibly tight.”.

“I think it was probably our best performance of the season, I thought we were terrific in the first half and could have scored two or three. Thierno [Barry] gets the goal again for us. There is a lot on his shoulders, he is our only recognised striker so hopefully he can keep putting the ball in the net like he has done. He is harsh on himself but his numbers are through the roof in terms of running. A clean sheet is massive for us. It is a long old season. We take it game by game but tonight feels good and we can look forward to Friday [against Coventry].”.

This was going to be a younger, more dynamic squad that would grow with the club as they looked to live up to the promise made by David Hopkinson, the chief executive, that they would be “consistently and credibly challenging” for top honours in England and Europe by 2030.

Having sold Bruno Guimarães (£73m), Sandro Tonali (£90m) and Anthony Gordon (£67m), Newcastle were able to spend roughly £262.9m on eight players to reinvigorate the squad as they once again talked about challenging for European qualification in Matthias Jaissle’s first season as manager.

It is always worth remembering that you only get a true reading of the Premier League table after ten games so this is a pivotal moment for both Newcastle and Everton as they play their ninth match of the campaign.

For Newcastle, a win tonight would take them up to seventh, just two points behind Chelsea in fourth. Despite the heavy away defeats and unconvincing performances, that would be an impressive start for a newly introduced manager. Matthias Jaissle has already felt the full force of the contrasting emotions on Tyneside in his three months in charge but major questions hang over his team. In particular, the “vertical football” style he brought from the Red Bull coaching school in Germany.

A defeat tonight, coming so soon after the 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup to Everton, will intensify the criticism of his approach. It would also suggest Newcastle, despite all their positive talk over the summer, are nothing more than a mid-table team who will be looking over their shoulders rather than upwards this season.

A win for Everton will have the same uplift for David Moyes at Everton, also taking them up to seventh in the table. Given all the problems attached to their summer recruitment - or rather the lack of it - Everton will have defied the grim pre-season predictions heading into the second international break. The table is starting to take shape and so are the narratives around every club.

Newcastle and Everton meet for the second time in matter of days as the Premier League weekend concludes in the north east at St James’ Park. These teams encountered each other on Thursday night in the League Cup, where Everton won 3-1 at the Hill Dickinson to progress to the quarter-finals in that competition.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle, who won 2-0 at Crystal Palace in their last league outing, come into this game in 12th, with the chance to rise to seventh with a victory tonight. Their boss Matthias Jaissle has called on his players to use the defeat against Everton on Thursday as fuel for tonight.

“Now it is about taking that frustration into motivation for Monday and having that approach for the rematch,” Jaissle said. “We take it as a long-term journey, and our approach is to make progress, to see improvements. Now it is time to learn fast out of the mistakes that we just did. [There are] other phases where we can already see that we improved and this is something we can count on, we can build on, the good part. But football is also in the end about results so you need to avoid these simple mistakes.”.

Everton, who have not won in the league since a 1-0 victory over Ipswich back in September, begin the night in 14th but, like Newcastle, could rise to seventh with a win. There are just two points that separate Bournemouth in seventh and Everton in 14th. Despite getting the better of Newcastle the other night, Everton manager David Moyes has warned that game will count for nothing tonight.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a different ball game,” Moyes mentioned. “Go to St James’ Park, on a Monday evening, they will get a crowd up there, you always know you are up against it. But we will go with confidence. We have played Newcastle a couple of times this year and done well, so we have to try and continue it. But Newcastle have got some really, really good players and players you have to concern yourself about.”.

Jack Grealish was left out of Everton’s squad for that League Cup victory because of an unauthorised absence from training and the 31-year-old is not expected to be involved tonight.

Recent findings suggest that these sides were involved in a dramatic fixture on this ground last season. Everton claimed a 3-2 victory, with Thierno Barry earning them all three points in the 83rd minute, moments after Jacob Murphy had equalised for Newcastle. Team news from St James’ Park to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A passionate Evertonian who has dedicated 60 years of her life to the NHS was recognised for her incredible contribution to health care when she was surprised at work by Blues legend Duncan Ferguson. Sheila Westhorp, 77, joined the A&E department at the Royal Liverpool University Hospital in the same month England’s recently-victorious World Cup hero Alan Ball moved to Everton from Blackpool in August 1966. Despite currently undergoing cancer treatment, Sheila refuses to step away from her role as a clerical officer – one that has seen her serve as a first point of contact for patients at three iterations of the Royal over six decades. Her remarkable longevity and dedication saw her nominated by colleagues for a special reward as part of a Hill Dickinson-sponsored initiative that recognises Blues working in the NHS. Sheila was stunned, then, to be greeted by one of her Everton favourites, armed with blue and white flowers and four tickets to enjoy an upcoming matchday in one of Hill Dickinson Stadium’s premium restaurants. There was a further surprise for Sheila when colleagues and ex-colleagues from her 60 years at the Royal poured into the room to join the celebrations. "I was absolutely gobsmacked," said Sheila. "That they got it past me in the first place, and then, when I walked in here, I thought 'I'm sure that's Duncan Ferguson'. Then I thought, 'don't be so stupid’! “I honestly can't believe it, and it means everything to me. I don't think I'm anything special - I just come here, try to be kind and do my job." Among the countless nominations Sheila received, colleagues applauded her resilience and determination in the face of her recent health complications, and the time and warmth she reserves for co-workers and patients alike. They also noted her unwavering love for Everton – a passion that also dates back to the 1960s when she first started attending fixtures at Goodison Park. Margaret Rogers, Administration Service Manager at the Royal, said: "Everything's a smile with Sheila, she just carries on regardless - she's proper old school, salt of the earth. She's always happy to chat, but always willing to listen. Everybody loves Sheila.” She added: “She loves Everton and she loves going to the games. It’s not just a passion for Sheila, it’s part of who she is.” As well as enjoying an upcoming fixture at Everton’s waterfront home, Sheila will be invited to a VIP experience later in the season, when she will go behind-the-scenes and watch the Men’s Senior team train, courtesy of Hill Dickinson. Everton Giant Ferguson, who scored 72 goals across 273 appearances for the Toffees and was this week appointed manager of Northern Irish club Glentoran, said: “Sheila’s a special person, a massive Evertonian and it’s an incredible feat to spend 60 years with the NHS. “It was fantastic meeting her, and I just feel proud and privileged to have come along and seen the amazing reaction she got from her friends and colleagues. It was truly deserved – well done, Sheila.” Andrew Craggs, Head of Health at Hill Dickinson, a commercial law firm and Everton's Official Stadium Naming Rights Partner, said: “The NHS continues to be home to countless examples of quiet, everyday heroism, and Sheila perfectly embodies the spirit of people working in NHS Trusts up and down the country. “It’s incredibly notable to us that Hill Dickinson Stadium has a positive impact in the community, so it’s our pleasure to be able to put together a unique experience for Sheila to enjoy with her loved ones to say thank you.” Evertonians who know an NHS hero can nominate them for a special surprise by completing the form here.

A passionate Evertonian who has dedicated 60 years of her life to the NHS was recognised for her incredible contribution to health care when she was surprised at work by Blues legend Duncan Ferguson.

Sheila Westhorp, 77, joined the A&E department at the Royal Liverpool University Hospital in the same month England’s recently-victorious World Cup hero Alan Ball moved to Everton from Blackpool in August 1966.

Despite at the moment undergoing cancer treatment, Sheila refuses to step away from her role as a clerical officer – one that has seen her serve as a first point of contact for patients at three iterations of the Royal over six decades.

Her remarkable longevity and dedication saw her nominated by colleagues for a special reward as part of a Hill Dickinson-sponsored initiative that recognises Blues working in the NHS.

Sheila was stunned, then, to be greeted by one of her Everton favourites, armed with blue and white flowers and four tickets to enjoy an upcoming matchday in one of Hill Dickinson Stadium’s premium restaurants.

There was a further surprise for Sheila when colleagues and ex-colleagues from her 60 years at the Royal poured into the room to join the celebrations.

"I was absolutely gobsmacked," noted Sheila. "That they got it past me in the first place, and then, when I walked in here, I thought 'I'm sure that's Duncan Ferguson'. Then I thought, 'don't be so stupid’!

Industry observers note that “I honestly can't believe it, and it means everything to me. I don't think I'm anything special - I just come here, try to be kind and do my job.".

Among the countless nominations Sheila received, colleagues applauded her resilience and determination in the face of her recent health concerns, and the time and warmth she reserves for co-workers and patients alike. They also noted her unwavering love for Everton – a passion that also dates back to the 1960s when she first started attending fixtures at Goodison Park.

She added: “She loves Everton and she loves going to the games. It’s not just a passion for Sheila, it’s part of who she is.”.

The in-form Pio Esposito is expected to continue leading the line for Inter as they take on VfB Stuttgart in the Champions League league phase on Wednesday evening.

Inter begin the day in 17th place in the Champions League table after recording two wins and two defeats across their first four league phase matches of the season.

The Nerazzurri picked up a 3-0 victory away against Feyenoord last time out in Europe and head into Wednesday’s tie off the back of a 4-4 draw away against Atalanta in Serie A over the weekend; Pio Esposito providing a hat-trick on the night. Cristian Chivu will be without two of his key midfielders in Hakan Calhanoglu and Piotr Zielinski this evening, which should mean opportunities for Petar Sucic and Curtis Jones along with Nicolo Barella. Hakan Calhanoglu and Aleksandar Stankovic are also available in midfield.

It has been revealed that captain and talisman Lautaro Martinez made his return from injury off the bench against Atalanta over the weekend, but it remains to be seen whether he is declared fit to start on Wednesday. Esposito and Marcus Thuram will be the go-to strike partnership if he isn’t.

Iranian activist and Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi shares her story in memoir

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1217 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.
  • "A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.
  • The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As PEN International marks Imprisoned Writer Day on November 15, a memoir by 2023 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi stands as a powerful act of resistance against authoritarian regimes.

"A Woman Never Stops Fighting — My Struggle for Freedom, Democracy and Human Rights in Iran," was recently published in German and is set to be released in English in September 2027.

The autobiography "portrays how Narges actually became the woman she is today — and it also reveals the price she had to pay to become that woman," Mariam Claren, spokesperson for the Narges Mohammadi Foundation Germany told DW.

Mohammadi wrote the autobiography in prison: "She was constantly writing," claims Claren, whose own mother, activist Nahid Taghavi, shared a cell with Mohammadi for two and a half years, in Iran's notorious Evin prison. "Then, in 2020, Narges was forcibly moved to another prison. All her documents were gone. And she had to start all over.".

But she managed to rewrite it all, and her texts were smuggled out of prison in fragments by fellow prisoners and visitors who risked their own safety.

In her memoir, Mohammadi recounts pivotal moments in her life, including her childhood and youth, how she started taking action against gender discrimination, political repression, the death penalty and human rights abuses, and the personal and emotional toll of her activism.

Recent findings suggest that the human rights activist has been sentenced to a combined total of more than 44 years in prison and 154 lashes. For more than a decade, she has been separated from her twin children, who are now 19 years old and live in exile in France for their own protection.

Born on April 21, 1972, in Zanjan, Iran, Narges Mohammadi became politically active while studying in physics at Imam Khomeini University of Qazvin in the 1990s.

In a recent development, in "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," she describes how she started mountain climbing as a student, and organized mixed-gender groups dedicated to mountaineering — a controversial initiative at the time. She also helped establish an independent student organization and advocated for political reform. Her activities led to repeated harassment and arrests by authorities.

She began her journalism career in 1996, writing about Iran's student and women's movements. As her public profile grew, she became increasingly involved in Iran's civil society and human rights community.

Sources indicate that in 1998, she married political activist Taghi Rahmani. The couple's twins, Ali and Kiana, were born in 2006.

Over the course of her career, Mohammadi worked with some of Iran's most prominent human rights organizations and became a leading figure in the Defenders of Human Rights Centre, founded by 2003 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Shirin Ebadi.

She played a key role in initiatives promoting free elections, peace and the abolition of the death penalty, especially for juvenile offenders. She also helped establish organizations supporting political prisoners and advocating for women's rights.

Her first major prison sentence related to her human rights activities came in 2011. It marked the beginning of a cycle of arrests and prosecutions that would define much of her adult life.

In her memoir, she describes an arrest that took place in front of her young children. At one point during her imprisonment, she lost the right to call them for several months.

She also details the brutal treatment she experienced in prison, with constant interrogations, beatings and denial of medical care.

Another central focus of her activism is denouncing the psychological effects of solitary confinement, which she had previously documented with fellow inmates in her book and documentary project "White Torture.".

It has been revealed that "When someone is subjected to physical torture, the scars, blood and infections — dreadful as they may be — serve as visible witnesses," she writes in her memoir. But, she adds, "when someone is subjected to psychological torture, no visible traces remain, and the victim cannot justify the trauma — neither to themselves nor to others. In fact, it becomes virtually impossible to even accept that one has been tortured at all, which causes the suffering to continue indefinitely.".

"This is also the goal of solitary confinement: to bring the imprisoned person to the very edge of nothingness — to strip them of their identity and of everything that makes them human," she writes.

Through her relentless campaigning against executions and state violence, she helped bring these problems to the forefront of public debate among Iranian activists.

International recognition of her work culminated in October 2023 when she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for "for her fight against the oppression of women in Iran and her fight to promote human rights and freedom for all.".

As Mohammadi was unable to attend the ceremony because she remained imprisoned in Tehran's Evin Prison, the award was accepted on her behalf by her teenage twins, who delivered her message to the world.

Following the Nobel Prize, Iranian authorities continued to pursue latest legal cases against her, restrict her communications and intensify pressure on her from prison.

She became the target of a systematic smear campaign, including widespread defamation, gender-based harassment and explicit death threats.

Sources indicate that "We are firmly convinced that the Islamic Republic of Iran has deployed its cyber army — which is the second-largest, after Russia's — to this end," says Claren of the Narges Mohammadi Foundation. Conspiracy theorists even started claiming she might be working for the regime, she adds: "And what is truly terrible about this is that when a lie is repeated over and over again and spread over the course of years, it eventually leads even ordinary people to start believing it.".

In late 2024, following surgery, Mohammadi was granted a temporary medical release. Doctors warned at the time that a return to prison could seriously endanger her health.

Nevertheless, Mohammadi was brutally arrested again in December 2025, while attending a memorial ceremony for Khosrow Alikordi, a lawyer and human rights activist who died in suspicious circumstances.

In prison, she was held in solitary confinement for an extended period and her health continued to deteriorate, Claren reports. But "thanks to a public campaign, she has now been granted what is known as an interruption of detention for medical reasons.".

But "that doesn't mean she is free," adds Claren, who notes that she still suffers from serious health problems — as do many Iranians who have been tortured in prison.

In February, an Iranian court ordered additional prison sentences for Mohammadi, along with a travel ban.

Sources indicate that mohammadi lives in constant fear of having to return to prison any day, notes Claren, and "this all comes with the pressure to which Iranian civil society — including, of course, people like Narges — is currently subjected, with questions like: Will Trump launch an attack, yes or no? Will there be another war?".

According to recent reports, despite this uncertainty, Mohammadi continues her activism. Her international profile also helps her supporters keep addressing publicly the issue of human rights in Iran in the public eye, says Claren: "It is incredibly important that, alongside the individual Narges Mohammadi, the focus also remains consistently on the struggle of the people in Iran for freedom, dignity, and fundamental rights — for the right to sing and dance.".

Latest Update: Could lack of money sink TFFF rainforest fund before it even releases?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1090 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.
  • More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.
  • According to recent reports, in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world's tropical forests play a vital role in slowing global heating and preserving biodiversity, storing climate-damaging carbon dioxide and providing a home for an extremely large number of species — when they're intact.

More than 140 countries committed to halting global deforestation by the end of the decade at the 2021 UN climate change conference in Glasgow, but five years later logging continues.

According to recent reports, in 2024, over 8 million hectares (19 million acres) of forest were lost. And since 1990, nearly 490 million hectares of forest have been wiped out.

Sources indicate that more recently, the trend has shifted in the opposite direction. Deforestation in the Amazon region of Brazil decreased by 41% from August 2025 through 2026 to reach its lowest rate since records began.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

To ensure lasting protection, the Tropical Forest Forever Facility was released in 2025 at the COP30 climate conference in Belem, Brazil.

Because rainforests are so key for the world, the idea behind the fund was to give money to the countries where they are located to help them preserve and protect these ecosystems.

So far, these countries have made more profit through deforestation — for example, by mining natural resources on rainforest land or farming the area.

Industry observers note that starting in 2027, the TFFF is expected to generate the funds needed for rainforest conservation, in part via contributions from various countries. By the end of this year, a total of $10 billion (€8.9 billion) in government capital is due to flow into the fund, mainly in the form of low-interest loans.

In addition, the TFFF is expected to concern bonds to private investors, such as banks and investment firms, to raise additional funds — initially totaling about $40 billion.

According to recent reports, going forward, the strategy is for governments to contribute a total of $25 billion to the pot, and for private donors to contribute $100 billion. The fund will then invest this money in international financial markets with the aim of generating profits.

Private investors who purchase TFFF bonds can expect to earn about 5% interest per bond per year, said Felix Finkbeiner, the founder of the German environmental organization Plant-for-the-Planet, where he is responsible for forest conservation and advocacy.

"Private investors' capital is very well protected," Finkbeiner said, adding that any losses the TFFF might incur on the capital markets — for example, if the price of its bonds should fall — would be offset by government funds.

About 2.7% of the TFFF's profits would be set aside for countries with tropical forests.

Countries would receive $4 per year for every hectare of forest that they preserve instead of chopping down. At least 20% of these funds must be allocated to Indigenous peoples and local communities.

According to calculations by the TFFF Watch website, an independent platform launched by Plant-for-the-Planet to track investments, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, would receive about $333 million for its 2024 forest stock under this system.

Recent findings suggest that finkbeiner said the subsidies would be paid only for intact ecosystems and not for timber plantations, with forest areas and their condition mapped and assessed using satellite imagery. Though it can sometimes be difficult to identify plantations accurately on satellite photos, he said, the technology has improved significantly over the last decade.

It has been revealed that that means any NGO or external party with access to the satellite data can check the condition of the region, providing further oversight. If forest areas are cleared or damaged, money is deducted from the total.

Another safeguard: If countries don't use the TFFF funds for rainforest conservation, their payments could be frozen for the next few years.

The TFFF is supposed to invest, whenever possible, in government bonds issued by emerging and developing countries. Above all, the idea is not to invest in projects that harm the climate — such as those linked to oil, gas, or coal investments.

The TFFF concept has received plenty of support from environmental organizations, in part because it gives countries in the Global South significantly more sovereignty than traditional forms of development financing.

"For example, if the government of Ghana wants to protect its rainforest today, it usually asks the World Bank for financial assistance — and then the World Bank in [Washington] DC decides whether Ghana is allowed to do so," Finkbeiner remarked.

The TFFF fund is also designed to be immune to donor countries' backing out in the event of a change in government, for example. Once a contribution is made, the money remains in the fund for 40 years before being paid back.

Recent findings suggest that continuing protection is also an incentive for countries receiving money from the fund. "When a new government comes into power that wants to cut back a little on climate protection, they will realize: We'll get more money if we protect the rainforest," said Finkbeiner.

For the rainforest fund to actually get off the ground, a total of $10 billion in seed capital must be raised by the end of 2026. So far, the confirmed pledges from countries, NGOs and foundations total only $7.9 billion.

Eight countries have expressed a willingness to contribute so far, including Brazil, Indonesia, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

Norway, with a pledge of $3 billion, is the largest would-be donor. However, the government in Oslo is willing to honor its commitment only if the agreed-upon total amount is in place by the end of the year.

"This deadline isn't set in stone, but otherwise the Norwegian government will have real trouble getting it through parliament," Finkbeiner said.

Germany's commitment must also still be approved by the parliament. The German government has pledged about €1 billion to the TFFF starting in 2027, to be paid out over 10 years.

Other countries are also considering investing in the TFFF, including Canada, China, South Korea and the United Arab Emirates.

Philanthropic organizations have pledged $88 million to the fund so far, including $73 million announced this week during the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Finkbeiner remains upbeat.

According to recent reports, "Promises like that always come at the last minute," he said. "I'm very optimistic that we'll secure more commitments at the COP — and in the course of December — and that we'll then reach that $10 billion.".

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With the controversy sparked by Felix Nmecha's celebrations after his goals in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elfersberg last weekend, the subject was always going to be top of reporters' minds when Germany coach Jürgen Klopp faced reporters ahead of Friday's match against Serbia.

Nmecha celebrated the goals by mimicking taking a crown off his head and kneeling to place it on the ground.

This was understood by many to be a nod to a Ballers in God (BIG) campaign called "The King's Return.".

According to recent reports, SIGNIFICANT, a Christian group for footballers, has remarked it aims to "demonstrate love and respect towards everyone," but critics claim it discriminates against the queer and transexual people. The discourse generated by the celebration did not go unnoticed by the Germany boss.

​Klopp told reporters in Belgrade on Thursday evening, that the 26-year-old Nmecha had assured him that he meant no harm by his actions.

It has been revealed that "Last weekend I ​saw Felix score two great goals and saw the celebration and then the gesture. I thought nothing of it at the time, but then it all kicked off," he mentioned.

"As the controversy escalated, I started looking into the details of the subject and trying to form a clear picture of it.

"I confronted him with all the things you (reporters) might have confronted him with. He told me that it had nothing to do with that at all, and that he loves all people and does not discriminate against anyone.".

He then said that Nmecha had agreed not to repeat the celebration.

Recent findings suggest that in Friday's match, Klopp's goal will be to keep alive Germany's chances of reaching the Nations League quarterfinals with a win over Serbia. Germany are third in Group A2 with 5 points, trailing the Netherlands and Greece, who both have 8. Serbia, who Germany beat 2-0 in Munich last month, are still without a win.

"We feel well prepared," Klopp said, adding that his team were committed to earning "a final" for the last group last group game on Monday in Berlin against the Netherlands.

According to recent reports, klopp also expressed his disappointment that only a few thousand Serbian children would be admitted to the stadium due to a spectator ban. Originally, the game was to be played behind closed doors after Serbia was sanctioned for racist and discriminatory behavior by its fans. However, a clause in the UEFA rules allows a selected group of guests to attend. Now children under 15 accompanied by teachers or football coaches are expected to be at the match.

Sources indicate that "We're expecting some 5,000 guests," a spokesman for the Serbian FA told the DPA news agency. The stadium's capacity is 55,000. The German FA has been allocated just 50 tickets for its fans.

Vignola Double Seals Victory For Blues

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, two outstanding goals from Ornella Vignola guided Everton to a comfortable win in the Subway Players Cup, as the Blues beat Newcastle United 2-0.
  • Two outstanding goals from Ornella Vignola guided Everton to a comfortable win in the Subway Players Cup, as the Blues beat Newcastle United 2-0.
  • After a goalless first half, Vignola came to the rescue for Everton with a long-range effort and curling strike being the difference at Goodison Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, two outstanding goals from Ornella Vignola guided Everton to a comfortable win in the Subway Players Cup, as the Blues beat Newcastle United 2-0. After a goalless first half, Vignola came to the rescue for Everton with a long-range effort and curling strike being the difference at Goodison Park. Everton now have consecutive wins in the cup after beating Birmingham City in their opening group stage game.Scott Phelan made nine changes to the team that faced London City Lionesses on Sunday, with Rion Ishikawa and Vignola being the two to keep their place in the starting XI. Noemie Mouchon and Jutta Rantala both made their long-awaited starts for the Club after the duo signed from Leicester City over the summer. In between the sticks, Canada’s Rylee Foster-Inman replaced Courtney Brosnan, making her second consecutive appearance in the Cup. Club captain, Megan Finnigan, returned to the pitch after missing Sunday’s clash in the capital, and was partnered alongside Hannah Silcock. After impressing from the bench in the last game, Aurora Galli started as well as Hannah Cain, who earned her spot in the lineup following her magnificent goal on the weekend. The Blues threatened early on down the left-hand side, and it was Cain who had the first opportunity of the match. Her effort whistled past the far post after she was picked out superbly by Silcock’s lofted, long-ball. 15 minutes into the first half, Everton were denied the lead after Mouchon’s first-time finish was ruled offside. The France-youth international was first to the rebound after Silcock tested Anna Tamminen from close range. Shortly after, Mouchon continued to cause problems for the Lasses, as she held up the ball in the center of the box and played a short pass to Cain, who struck the post with a side-footed effort. Scott Phelan was able to talk to his players 28 minutes into the game after Newcastle’s Leanne Kiernan suffered a knock, and the pressure continued to pile on the away side for the remainder of the first 45 minutes. Minutes before the end of the first half, Tamminen was yet again called upon as she parried away Vignola’s long-range strike. The first half drew to a close, with the Toffees looking to break the deadlock in the second 45 minutes. Newcastle were forced to substitute Tamminen for Kayla Rendell after the break, whilst Blues keeper, Foster-Inman, did not have to make a save until 52 minutes. Whilst Newcastle began to counter-attack effectively, The Blues were still creating the more clear-cut chances. Cain was again at the forefront of Everton attacks, and her whipped cross found Galli on the edge of the box, but her effort blazed over the crossbar on the hour mark. With the game still goalless, Phelan looked to the bench for reinforcements and brought on Clare Wheeler, Maz Pacheco, and Yuka Momiki. But it was Vignola who took the lead for the Blues. Her fantastic long-range effort from outside the box rifling into the top-right corner, leaving Kayla Rendell rooted to the spot. With 10 minutes to go, the Spain international added a second after Wheeler’s cut-back cross found Everton's number 18 unmarked. Her tidy finish into the bottom right-hand corner eliminated any chance of a nervy end to proceedings, as Everton continued to pass the ball around nicely for the remainder of the game. Following six minutes of stoppage time, the final whistle sounded to confirm an impressive second-half display from Everton. After two consecutive wins in the Player Cup, and five on home soil in all competitions, the Blues will now have their eye on automatic qualification for the next round. Phelan's side return to the Grand Old Lady on Sunday afternoon (2pm) as Aston Villa make the journey from the second city. Tickets can be purchased here.

Two outstanding goals from Ornella Vignola guided Everton to a comfortable win in the Subway Players Cup, as the Blues beat Newcastle United 2-0.

After a goalless first half, Vignola came to the rescue for Everton with a long-range effort and curling strike being the difference at Goodison Park.

Everton now have consecutive wins in the cup after beating Birmingham City in their opening group stage game.

Scott Phelan made nine changes to the team that faced London City Lionesses on Sunday, with Rion Ishikawa and Vignola being the two to keep their place in the starting XI.

Noemie Mouchon and Jutta Rantala both made their long-awaited starts for the Club after the duo signed from Leicester City over the summer.

In between the sticks, Canada’s Rylee Foster-Inman replaced Courtney Brosnan, making her second consecutive appearance in the Cup.

Club captain, Megan Finnigan, returned to the pitch after missing Sunday’s clash in the capital, and was partnered alongside Hannah Silcock.

After impressing from the bench in the last game, Aurora Galli started as well as Hannah Cain, who earned her spot in the lineup following her magnificent goal on the weekend.

Sources indicate that the Blues threatened early on down the left-hand side, and it was Cain who had the first opportunity of the match. Her effort whistled past the far post after she was picked out superbly by Silcock’s lofted, long-ball.

Industry observers note that 15 minutes into the first half, Everton were denied the lead after Mouchon’s first-time finish was ruled offside. The France-youth international was first to the rebound after Silcock tested Anna Tamminen from close range.

Shortly after, Mouchon continued to cause problems for the Lasses, as she held up the ball in the center of the box and played a short pass to Cain, who struck the post with a side-footed effort.

Scott Phelan was able to talk to his players 28 minutes into the game after Newcastle’s Leanne Kiernan suffered a knock, and the pressure continued to pile on the away side for the remainder of the first 45 minutes.

Minutes before the end of the first half, Tamminen was yet again called upon as she parried away Vignola’s long-range strike.

The first half drew to a close, with the Toffees looking to break the deadlock in the second 45 minutes.

Newcastle were forced to substitute Tamminen for Kayla Rendell after the break, whilst Blues keeper, Foster-Inman, did not have to make a save until 52 minutes.

Whilst Newcastle began to counter-attack effectively, The Blues were still creating the more clear-cut chances.

Cain was again at the forefront of Everton attacks, and her whipped cross found Galli on the edge of the box, but her effort blazed over the crossbar on the hour mark.

With the game still goalless, Phelan looked to the bench for reinforcements and brought on Clare Wheeler, Maz Pacheco, and Yuka Momiki.

It has been revealed that but it was Vignola who took the lead for the Blues. Her fantastic long-range effort from outside the box rifling into the top-right corner, leaving Kayla Rendell rooted to the spot.

With 10 minutes to go, the Spain international added a second after Wheeler’s cut-back cross found Everton's number 18 unmarked.

Her tidy finish into the bottom right-hand corner eliminated any chance of a nervy end to proceedings, as Everton continued to pass the ball around nicely for the remainder of the game.

Following six minutes of stoppage time, the final whistle sounded to confirm an impressive second-half display from Everton.

After two consecutive wins in the Player Cup, and five on home soil in all competitions, the Blues will now have their eye on automatic qualification for the next round.

Phelan's side return to the Grand Old Lady on Sunday afternoon (2pm) as Aston Villa make the journey from the second city.

💡 Key Takeaways
