  • Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.
  • Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:46 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:51 EST, 24 November 2026.

Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee in a hard-fought contest at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden – who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box – had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee, still licking their wounds after an 8-0 savaging at the hands of Hearts on Saturday, indicated plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Manager Marink Reedijk was thrilled to have bounced back from their 4-0 weekend home defeat at the hands of Dundee United, saying: ‘I think it’s a good reaction to what we have done against Dundee United.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s important that you get the three points at home. Again, that’s a major win. I saw a front foot team again, I saw togetherness again, I saw a team who fought for every ball.

Martin Boyle takes the acclaim after scoring the all-important second goal for Hibernian.

‘That’s not easy, they have to be patient, you have to be secure, you have to wait for your moment and we took these moments and that was really good to see.

‘The goal of Nicky [Cadden] is one to, we say, put in a frame and put on your wall as a painting. The one of Martin [Boyle] is why Martin is so key for us. He can disrupt an opponent if they are so organised and so close to each other and so deep.

‘As long as we keep ourselves, I think these are good signs.’.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend. On a rare start, Togo international Thibault Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan’s lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Sources indicate that dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them with two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Nicky Cadden unleashes an absolute pearler into the top corner to put Hibs in front.

Industry observers note that cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Steven Pressley’s side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones’ free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

For Pressley, who changed half of his outfield XI following his side’s weekend humiliation, there were also positives to take.

Industry observers note that the Dark Blues boss noted: ‘We’re disappointed to not come away with anything and to obviously lose the game. But I also thought we restored some degree of pride tonight.

‘Going into half-time 2-0 down, losing two late goals in the half, can be a little bit demoralising, especially for a team that has a bit of fragility on the back of the weekend’s result.

It has been revealed that ‘I thought we responded brilliantly. We revealed a lot of courage, a lot of determination, a lot of spirit and, as I’ve said, I think we certainly restored some level of pride that allows us a foundation to move into the weekend.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Original Article was published on 23 September 2026.

Correction to: Nature https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-11007-3 Published online 23 September 2026.

In the version of the article initially published, in the Abstract, “Biogeography” section and Conclusion, the epoch in which bats originated was given as the “late Palaeocene” but should have been “late Cretaceous/early Palaeocene”. This has now been corrected in the HTML and PDF versions of this article.

Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?
  • At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.
  • According to recent reports, roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

According to recent reports, roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

United fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

In a recent development, whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Industry observers note that carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

In a recent development, he had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

NO MISTAKE THIS TIME 💪 Bruno Fernandes gets United back in it after a penalty retake 😤 https://t.co/uQdkNs0lXo.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

Sources indicate that from being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

It has been revealed that IT'S 2-2! 💥 Cunha levels it up for United! 🔴🇧🇷 https://t.co/q60oQUoat1.

At that point, the momentum was firmly in United’s favour and three minutes later they were in front. It is a source of bemusement among fans that Shea Lacey has not had more game-time considering how poor some senior players have been. And his arrival as a substitute made a big difference.

It was Lacey who speared an inch-perfect pass into Cunha, who turned sharply before drilling a stunning finish in off the near post. Cue bedlam.

Sources indicate that MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 https://t.co/ATD8wDlc1e.

Cunha was booked for taking off his shirt as he crowd-surfed bear-chested among the fans and was then sent off minutes later after a poor challenge. A fittingly chaotic end to a crazy night for the match-winner.

The difference to those opening 45 minutes was as stark as it gets. Indeed, the first half felt like a continuation from the fans of their blood-letting against Bournemouth.

According to recent reports, when the clock hit 20.05 – a nod to the year 2005 when the Glazers bought the club – a pile of tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch from the Stretford End amid chants of “We Want Glazers Out”. They were quickly followed by cries of “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” and “sell the club and f--- off home”.

Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, again copped for it. A banner read: “For the love, not the ‘likes’”. When the Champions League music played, hundreds of green and gold balloons – a reference to the club’s original colours and the 2010 protest movement – were released.

Industry observers note that on the pitch, United were all over the place. Carrick had dropped Lisandro Martínez after his red card against Chelsea but his replacement Ayden Heaven was at fault for the first goal after getting sucked in and failing to check his shoulder. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬 United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 https://t.co/DtIOFJYZ6D.

Heaven almost did the same again soon after before more blunders handed Roma a second. Soulé tried to find Donyell Malen with a pass but miscued to Harry Maguire. Yet the England defender then proceeded to give the ball straight back to Soulé, who turned Dalot and shot with Heaven blocking the ball with his right arm as he lunged to stop the effort. Malen continued his rich scoring vein from the penalty spot.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box 😬 https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES.

At that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

“It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” stated Carrick.

“I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

According to recent reports, asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

Industry observers note that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys demonstrated an awful lot,” he mentioned.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he showed everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

It has been revealed that “But today was important to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

Industry observers note that “It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

Sources indicate that “It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, massive character, big fight.”.

“We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

As for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we indicated what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

For the badge ✊🇾🇪 https://t.co/BOGdZRmkiZ.

Sources indicate that “Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time. They were everywhere in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things,” Alan Shearer said after the final whistle.

“I said what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker, and run in behind and they did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.”.

Possession: United 52% vs 48% Roma.

Touches in opposition box: 30 vs 8.

For the first time in months, United fans have witnessed a performance worth cheering (at least in the second half).

As Michael Carrick led his players around the pitch – with the occasional smile and fist pump – they were all greeted by cheers and applause in the stands. Some of them might have forgotten what that was like.

MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 https://t.co/ATD8wDlc1e.

There is no guarantee that this is enough to keep Michael Carrick in a job beyond the November international break, but if he keeps his role, this will certainly be a turning point.

We will have to wait until Amazon release their All or Nothing documentary to find out what he said to them in the dressing room at half time but whatever it was, it worked.

Manchester United finally have their win!

Final seconds and Roma are pushing for an equaliser. Pisilli sends a cross in but Yoro heads it away.

Roma come again, but Mount wellies it half the length of the pitch to huge cheers.

The United team that went into the dressing room at half time did not look like they had a second half like this in them.

They almost throw it away as Cristante loops a ball into the box for Castro to head, but the striker connects poorly and sends it wide. He was also offside anyway.

According to recent reports, well Cunha has absolutely lost his head there. Booked for taking his shirt off just minutes ago, he goes in for a ridiculous late challenge and wipes out Balerdi. The ref quickly produces a yellow and Cunha is off!

United will have to see out the final minutes with 10 men.

This is the energy that United have been looking for over the last few months, and wouldn’t you know that they’re about to reap the rewards.

IT'S 2-2! 💥 Cunha levels it up for United! 🔴🇧🇷 https://t.co/q60oQUoat1.

Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire come off, replaced by Mason Mount and Matthias de Ligt.

Probbably around six minutes to go here with the added time.

Incredible strike from Mateus Cunha to complete an astonishing second-half performance!

He picks up the ball from Lacey as he dashes into the box and looks up to see just a whisker of space at the near post and puts his foot through the ball!

He then takes of his shirt and debuts himself into the crowd...

United have easily had the better of the second half and could take something from this.

Industry observers note that maguire goes down under pressure by Castro and tries to shield the ball and ends up in a tussle with the Roma striker. No cards given luckily for Maguire.

Industry observers note that and a bit of luck finally goes United’s way! A defensive blunder from Roma as Bruno Fernandes curls a ball into the box and Balerdi completely misses the ball as he tries to clear it from the box. Cunha is lurking behind him and turns the ball into the next low from close range.

Yoro passes the ball in to Mainoo on the edge of the area and he tries a back-heel, but there is no team-mate there to meet it and Roma bring the ball out again.

United intercept in midfield again, which is where the game has turned in the second half and they come again.

10 minutes plus added time left. United are still fighting for an equaliser here to their credit, but waiting until they were two goals down to start battling made it very hard for them.

Sources indicate that another Roma change, and it’s Donyell Malen making way for Santiago Castro. He will end tonight with just the one goal.

Seconds after stepping on the pitch, he gets in a tangle with Maguire and the England defender gets booked for bringing him dowm.

Cunha has a powerful attempt that’s parried away by Vásquez and collected by Lacey.

Plenty of shouts for a foul as he tries to cross the ball in, but the referee is unmoved to give a penalty.

It’s Ayden Heaven that makes way for Lisandro Martínez, while Amad Diallo comes off for Shea Lacey.

It has been revealed that roma making changes of their own. Mancini and Hermoso are replaced by Daniele Ghilardi and Evan Ndicka – two straight defensive swaps.

Industry observers note that yoro intercepts a ball in midfield and finds Bruno Fernandes. He tries to tee up Diallo but the winger loses the ball from another well-timed Roma challenge.

Sources indicate that united look like they’re getting ready to make some changes... and it looks like Martínez is one of them.

Tielemans tries to set Diallo free with a long ball but there’s too much on it and Vásquez comes to collect.

NO MISTAKE THIS TIME 💪 Bruno Fernandes gets United back in it after a penalty retake 😤 https://t.co/uQdkNs0lXo.

It has been revealed that roma trying again down but Cunha dispossesses Lulli, trying to release Bruno Fernandes. Lulli gets back to make the challenge and stop the run.

It has been revealed that heaven is booked for a challenge, going in high. These kinds of tackles were utterly missing from United in the first half, even if the young defender will have to be careful now.

In a recent development, maguire and Balerdi wrestling at the back post, and the defender isn’t even watching the ball as Maguire tries to get his head on it. He gets away from the defender but is falling as he connects with the ball and it goes over the bar.

It causes chaos as Maguire heads the ball back into the box from the near post and as Vásquez tries to fall on it, Cristante tries to kick it away, meaning it bounces around the box.

Another corner for United from the throw-in.

Huge shouts for a penalty as Bruno Fernandes whips it in from the left to the near post where Mbeumo can’t connect but it goes out for a corner.

Maguire muscles away his defender at the back post and gets a clean header which is just blocked by Wesley for another corner.

Sources indicate that united have kept themselves in this game just about and for the first time all night the Roma fans are drowned out. The stands are willing their team on again as they try and pull the ball forward.

Dalot picks up the ball on the left midfield and he makes the run into the box and has a shot that just edges wide of the near post.

There is so much more life now in United.

Eight games for Bruno Fernandes without a goal or assist but he has finally broken that drought.

It took a bit of luck, as one of the Roma defenders encroached on the area before the penalty was taken, which was deemed to allow him to have reached the ball to clear it after the save.

NO MISTAKE THIS TIME 💪 Bruno Fernandes gets United back in it after a penalty retake 😤 https://t.co/uQdkNs0lXo.

And now the floodgates have opened!

Mbeumo chases onto a ball from Cunha and the keeper comes out to meet him but he slots it past him...only to be denied by both the posts!

He can’t believe it and neither can Carrick.

But Old Trafford has woken up now!

And he makes it second time of asking!!

What a relief that will be for the captain. No mistake this time he puts his head down and wraps the inside of his foot around it!

Now there’s a check for encroachment and it’s confirmed! Another lifeline!

In a recent development, it’s given and Bruno Fernandes steps up to take it. A long wait for the whistle and a deep breath and he tries to go low to Vásquez’s right but the keeper guesses right. The rebound is cleared away before he can try again.

Cunha goes over in the box and the ref points to the spot.

Sources indicate that he exchanges a give-and-go with Bruno Fernandes but goes down supposedly under pressure by Mancini. In the replay it looks like he trips over his own feet though..

Industry observers note that diallo picks up the ball on the right and tries to get it in to Yoro who makes the run into the box. It’s not quite right though and Roma clear.

Some small signs of life here from United!

Roma try a long ball to Malen but Maguire and Heaven are equal to it and Maguire comes away with it.

He tries a long ball of his own towards Cunha making the run on the left but Lulli sticks close to him and gives him no space to pull the ball back form the touchline.

That is so disappointing for Baleba as Tielemens does take is place.

He goes straight down the tunnel, handing his jersey to a young fan on the way.

Yoro and Bruno Fernandes try to create some space with a give-and-go but Yoro is blocked and Roma pick up the ball again.

Sources indicate that that was the first moment a United player highlighted some initiative in 47 minutes of football. He is limping around the field and it looks like Youri Tielemens will replace him, but for now United are down to 10 men.

Baleba makes a lovely run in behind, driving into the six-yard box and reaching the byline looking like he will cross but then suddenly pulls up and goes down clutching his hamstring.

Rodrigo Mora is off and Niccolo Pisilli comes on in his place.

The latest scores from around the Champions League:.

Possession: United 54% vs 46% Roma.

Touches in opposition box: 11 vs 8.

Alan Shearer does not have kind words at half-time for the United squad, labelling the performance “embarrassing”:.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s not been anything in this performance. I haven’t seen a tackle, a cross, an effort at goal. There is nothing in this performance to be positive about.

“I don’t know where [Carrick] starts because they have been that poor in every department.

“Defensively all over the place, midfield no creativity, and up front no running in behind, no efforts at goal, no holding the ball up. It’s really been embarrassing for them.”.

The last action of the half is another Roma chance, which goes just wide of the top corner.

Boos ring out around Old Trafford as the whistle goes and the players trudge off.

What on earth can Carrick say to his squad to get them to turn this around?

Industry observers note that two minutes of added time begin with Cunha winning a free-kick. Bruno Fernandes passes a short ball forward to Mainoo just outside the area and he has a shot on goal with a neat ball which just dips. Vásquez gets across to collect.

Malen gets another go on goal, finding space down the centre to take a low shot at Lammens, but the keeper is equal to it and gets low to make the save.

Almost something, perhaps a hint of life from United.

According to recent reports, baleba tees up Diallo neatly to make a run into the box but he runs out of room and has to turn the ball back out to Baleba, who first time passes it along the edge of the area. Bruno Fernandes tries to get onto it but it’s an awkward first-time ball and it goes over the bar.

The Roma fans are in loud voice as United again try to progress in the final third.

Malen is booked as Baleba knocks it past him and is hauled down. It’s a decent position to have an attempt on goal, about 35 yards out against a relatively untested keeper.

In a recent development, bruno Fernandes sends it straight into the wall though. A thoroughly underwhelming attempt.

According to recent reports, roma are going forward again, finding space everywhere they look. They pass the ball from left to midfield and out to the right before it comes back to the left, and Mora finds himself on the edge of the area unmarked. A last-ditch challenge from Yoro is the only thing that denies him a shot and United concede a corner.

Sources indicate that mbeumo passes in to Mainoo from the right wing and he makes a run towards the edge of the box but is met by a tight defense. United are not having any luck down the middle and do not look particularly comfortable on the wings.

Baleba wins a free-kick as he is brought down by Cristante. Bruno Fernandes loops a cute ball into the box for Cunha to run onto but Cristante makes another good challenge to get him off the ball.

Roma have hardly put a foot wrong so far.

According to recent reports, balerdi does well to recover the ball as Mbeumo beats him to a header and takes the ball towards the box. The Roma defender makes another very well-timed challenge in the box to deny the striker a chance.

United just aren’t getting forward, they look out of ideas already.

Roma are pressing high on the ball, giving themselves a lot of options to get the ball forward.

Bruno Fernandes is trying to get his team-mates to make runs forward whne they have the ball but Diallo and Mbeumo aren’t quite firing.

Recent findings suggest that lulli and Soulé by contrast are finding a lot of joy down the right wing. Lulli sends a ball over the box but with too much on it, no one can connect at the back post.

Kobbie Mainoo dances away from two Roma players very tidily, protecting the ball in his own half.

United are trying to get the ball forward but just aren’t finding any space.

In a recent development, chants of “Jason Wilcox is a w-----” and “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” also reverberating. United ownership and executives under constant bombardment.

Cristante tries to send a cross into the box but it takes a looping deflection and is hauled away.

Maguire tries to set Diallo free in the next passage of play but he can’t bring down the long ball sent his way in midfield.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been plans to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No fresh stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no new concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

It’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Lisandro Martinez is shown a second yellow card following a VAR review 🟥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max ➡️https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/VLcAMNdqgZ.

All in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. If the beleaguered manager has any hope at all of hanging on to his job, he needs convincing results tonight and against Aston Villa on the weekend.

Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

Recent findings suggest that the visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They got off to a slow start in Europe, drawing with Fernebahce in their opening match but coming agonisingly close to stunning Real Madrid on matchday two at home. They went 3-1 up before three late goals snatched victory for Madrid.

It has been revealed that they bounced back with a convincing 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava and their domestic campaign is off to an incredibly promising start. They are right now unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

Industry observers note that it has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Feel free to drop us your score predictions in the comments – bragging rights on the line for the winner.

We’ll be bringing you team news, previews from the managers and more ahead of kick-off at 8pm!

Ice hockey impasse as Russia threatens sanctions on Canada, Germany

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.
  • "There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak noted after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Should Canada and Germany refuse to allow the Russian team to participate, we will demand compensation, enforce the postponement of the competitions, and impose sanctions on the organizers," Russian Ice Hockey Federation President Vladislav Tretiak told the TASS news agency.

"There are rules: if a team does not take the ice, it receives a forfeit loss and sanctions are imposed," Tretiak noted after a presidential sports council meeting in Moscow on Thursday.

"The IIHF as a way out — either allow us to participate or, if we cannot enter Canada, move the championship, don't hold it at all, or impose sanctions on Canada.".

The threat comes after the Canadian government confirmed Wednesday that it would not allow Russian players to take part in the IIHF World Junior Championship starting on December 26 in Alberta.

"Canada's position is unequivocal: as long as Russia continues ⁠its war of aggression ​against Ukraine, there can be no return to business as usual," Adam van Koeverden, Canada's secretary of sport, mentioned in a statement on Wednesday. "Canada will continue to stand with Ukraine.".

Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling in late October, in which it said the security concerns the IIHF cited for barring Russian teams from taking part in international tournaments was not sufficient, the world governing body pledged to work to comply with the decision.

According to recent reports, on November 8, Norway stated it had been bumped from the World Juniors tournament and had been informed by the IIHF that Russia would take its place. Several other national hockey associations said they had received a revised schedule for the tournament and stated they would not play against Russia. The IIHF has not confirmed the change.

Germany has been watching developments related to the World Juniors and host nation Canada closely, as it is set to host the IIHF World Championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf starting on May 14.

With several nations saying they will not play Russia and major sponsors threatening to pull out, a German government spokesman described the prospect of hosting the tournament under these conditions as "effectively impossible.".

However, Germany has ruled out taking the Canadian approach.

Ronald Rauhe, Germany's minister of state for sport, said Wednesday that refusing to grant visas was "not a solution for the [German] ice hockey federation [DEB], nor is it a solution for successfully hosting a world championship anywhere.".

At the same time, though, he expressed support for the DEB in its wish to host the tournament as planned.

"We believe that we should channel all our energy and efforts into helping sport — and ice hockey in particular — find a solution, which would, of course, entail excluding Russia from the World Championship.".

What makes things even more complicated for German officials are concerns that taking a hard-line on Russia could jeopardize Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

According to recent reports, the thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees bidding to host an Olympic Games to follow its lead. The IOC is set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process.

According to recent reports, for now, though, the ball appears to be in the IIHF's court, after Ottawa confirmed its refusal to grant Russians visas to play in the World Juniors. How the dispute regarding that tournament gets resolved could go a long way to finding a solution for the men's tournament in Germany in May.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was not best pleased after full-time of Manchester City’s 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday evening after hearing insults and chants directed at his family.

It has been revealed that napoli were praised for their performance away against Man City on Tuesday night, picking up a useful 2-2 draw against the European heavyweights despite their rocky form across the first few months of the 2026-27 season. The Partenopei took the lead twice on the night through Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, but were dealt equalisers by Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki; all four goals coming in the second half.

It wasn’t the most pleasant evening for Italy national team goalkeeper Donnarumma, who lined up in goal for the hosts. He was born in Castellammare di Stabia in Naples and has previously admitted that members of his family are Napoli supporters.

When Manchester City hosted Napoli in the Champions League last season, Donnarumma’s first start in the competition after joining from PSG, the stopper admitted that he had left his mother to watch from home given her conflict of interest.

After full-time on Tuesday evening, Italian reporters in the mixed zone asked Donnarumma how his mother was doing after the 2-2 draw between the two sides at The Etihad. “I’m angry because they insulted me,” noted a visibly angered Donnarumma while making his way out of the room.

According to the Corriere dello Sport, Donnarumma was repeatedly subjected to insulting chants from the Napoli fans during Tuesday’s game, and was called a ‘son of a b****’ on several occasions by the travelling supporters.

Detailed travel advice is right now being developed, including information on rail services, replacement transport where applicable and alternative ways of travelling to and from the stadium. Supporters do not need to make any changes to their travel plans at this stage. Detailed information will be provided well in advance of the fixture as arrangements are confirmed. With the match taking place on a Friday evening, supporters will also be encouraged to allow additional time for their journey and to check the latest travel information before setting off. Everton and Merseyrail recognise the importance of providing supporters with clear and timely information and will continue to work together, alongside the Liverpool City Region Combined Authority and other transport partners, to support safe and effective travel to and from the fixture. Further updates will be published through evertonfc.com, Merseyrail channels and Liverpool City Region transport information services as arrangements are confirmed.

#118195. What's going on with the polar vortex?

What's going on with the polar vortex?

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons.
  • If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.
  • Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

High up in the atmosphere, there's a ring of cold air swirling over the Arctic that can intensify, weaken, and shapeshift through the seasons. This is the polar vortex.

If it gets disrupted, this twisting pool of chilly air can influence the weather we experience, increasing the risk of a cold snap in the Northern Hemisphere.

Current observations show the vortex has weakened unprecedentedly early this year, with its winds reversing directions.

It's not yet clear how the current disruption to the polar vortex will affect the Northern Hemisphere winter, but scientists agree it is a record-breaking event.

"As far as we know, this is the earliest stratospheric vortex disruption that has been observed," European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecast (ECMWF) principal scientists Tim Stockdale and Frederic Vitart told the AFP news agency.

The French meteorological agency Meteo-France, meanwhile, called it "an unprecedented event.".

The early breakdown of the vortex "really increases the chance of cold air outbreaks across the latitudes where most of the densely populated population centers are across the Northern Hemisphere, US, Europe and East Asia," Judah Cohen, a climatologist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology told AFP.

The polar vortex is an enormous band of cold, low-pressure air that spins counterclockwise around the North Pole, about 10 to 50 kilometers (around 6 to 30 miles) above the surface.

Sources indicate that it's closely connected to the jet stream, another band of powerful winds just below the vortex. The jet stream forms a boundary where the cold Arctic air meets warmer air from the tropics and subtropics.

The vortex can sometimes be a tight circle, keeping the coldest air locked around the North Pole over winter. It can also form uneven waves that dip southwards. And as it changes in strength and shape, that can influence the atmosphere below and alter the position of the jet stream, which drives the weather on the ground.

So, if the jet stream is more "wavy," and plunges south, it may also allow freezing Arctic air to spill southward.

One of the biggest influences that can provoke this kind of disruption is known as "sudden stratospheric warming." This is when temperatures in the polar stratosphere rise dramatically within a few days, causing the vortex's strong westerly winds to weaken.

This can push the vortex off its spot at the North Pole, make it split apart into multiple rings, or — as is happening now — cause the westerly winds to change direction.

It can take several weeks for the vortex to recover.

A previous polar vortex disruption contributed to the deadly Great Texas Freeze in February 2021, which caused more than a week of freezing temperatures that sparked power outages and killed hundreds of people.

But bone-chilling cold isn't a foregone conclusion. The Met Office, which is the UK's national weather and climate service, stresses that what's happening with the polar vortex can nudge odds in that direction, but it's not a switch that turns cold weather on and off.

Other weather patterns can also influence the outcome.

Recent findings suggest that for example, there's a possibility El Nino, which is associated with milder winters, could "moderate or modify" the impacts, Cohen told AFP. But he added this was not certain.

The El Nino weather phenomenon, caused by the warming of surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, is currently intensifying and is expected to peak at the end of the year. The ongoing event has been classified as exceptionally strong and is disrupting weather around the globe.

Recent findings suggest that some research has also linked the rapid warming of the Arctic driven by climate change to increasing disruptions to the polar vortex. That means that, even as the planet warms, some areas may still experience more severe cold spells. But this connection is not conclusive and is still debated by scientists.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pep Guardiola claims that it was ‘one of the greatest honours’ to be considered for the role of Italy national team head coach during Paolo Maldini’s brief reign as technical director of the FIGC and says that he ‘probably would have accepted’ had the offer come a year or two later down the line.

Guardiola, along with Carlo Ancelotti and then later Andrea Pirlo, were among the names that Maldini had sought to appoint as head coach of the Italy national team during his brief reign as technical director of the FIGC over the summer.

In the end, neither Guardiola nor Ancelotti were available, Pirlo’s appointment was blocked, and Maldini decided to step down from his position with the Italian FA after just 16 days at the helm. Maldini was then replaced by Claudio Ranieri and Roberto Mancini has since returned as CT.

Guardiola, speaking in an interview his former Barcelona teammate Romario on his eponymous YouTube channel, mentioned that it was one of the biggest honours of his career to be considered for the Italy job and admitted that had he not needed a sabbatical, he ‘probably would have accepted’ the Azzurri offer.

In a recent development, “It’s the first time I’ve spoken about it, but yes, I spoke with them,” Guardiola told Romario. “It was an honour. I felt embarrassed saying no to a country or squad like Italy. It was one of the greatest honours I’ve ever had, that they thought of me to be the coach of Italy, but I realised I had to stop.

“If they’d approached me a year or two later, I probably would have accepted.

“They approached, with Paolo Maldini and Leonardo, whom I love dearly, at a time where I needed to take a break and come to Bahia to spend more time for myself. It’s been 18 years of coaching games every three days, three days, three days. You have to win trebles, play every three days, play every three days. And then there was a moment when I stated ‘oof’ [enough].”.

At 32, however, his next contract decision is extremely key.

Recent findings suggest that united need to show Fernandes that the club can still match his ambitions. Results have been poor, contract talks are paused and Sporting will always offer an emotional alternative.

Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1100 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when police officers appeared at her home in Istanbul last Wednesday evening, Yonca Verdioglu Sik was surprised — even more so when they took her in for questioning.
  • But, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage.
  • Recent findings suggest that for 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when police officers appeared at her home in Istanbul last Wednesday evening, Yonca Verdioglu Sik was surprised — even more so when they took her in for questioning. Her lawyer indicates she was accused of political and military espionage.

But, according to transcripts of the interrogation that were published later, Verdioglu Sik was never asked any questions about espionage. Instead the public prosecutor's office appeared to be more interested in the activities of her German employer, the Heinrich Böll Foundation.

Recent findings suggest that for 18 years, Verdioglu Sik, who was born and raised in Germany, has been the foundation's project coordinator. In her role, she organizes projects that focus on democracy and the rights of women, minorities and LGBTQ+ people.

During the interrogation, transfers of money from the foundation into her bank account were discussed. Verdioglu Sik found out that she was now also subject to a travel ban.

Verdioglu Sik was eventually released, but her arrest caused outrage among critics of the Turkish government. She is married to investigative journalist and member of parliament, Ahmet Sik. He belongs to the left-wing Workers' Party of Turkey, or TIP, and is known as one of the harshest critics of the current government.

Sik has recently been looking into a stock market scandal, which allegedly benefited members of the ruling Justice and Development Party, or AKP, headed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and associates.

Recent findings suggest that opposition critics drew a clear conclusion: As a member of parliament, Sik has parliamentary immunity. So instead, the justice system is putting pressure on him through his wife.

"If you take away a state's law, what is left is no longer called a state, but a gang," Sik responded to the arrest in writing.

According to recent reports, verdioglu Sik's arrest is not the first such case in Turkey. Ever since the attempted coup against the Erdogan government in 2016, accusations of espionage have been leveled at a wide variety of groups in Turkey: journalists, opposition figures and human rights activists as well as employees of foreign embassies and staff of foreign institutions like nongovernmental organizations and foundations.

In a recent development, such accusations have often been followed by acquittals or convictions for other offenses, albeit sometimes years later. But what the many instances have in common is what's known as a "chilling effect." Any investigation can mean lengthy pre-trial detention, reputational and professional damage and even social isolation.

In the past, such cases have even triggered diplomatic spats.

In 2015, for example, Can Dundar and Erdem Gul, both senior journalists at the opposition daily Cumhuriyet, were accused of espionage after reporting that Turkey had tried to ship arms to rebels fighting the Syrian government. Dundar now lives in exile in Berlin.

In 2017, Erdogan remarked that reporter Deniz Yücel, then working for German newspaper Die Welt, was a "German agent." That led to a serious diplomatic crisis between Berlin and Ankara.

Industry observers note that espionage charges have also been laid against local employees of the US diplomatic corps and against a lawyer working for the German embassy. US pastor Andrew Brunson and his wife were also arrested because of alleged links to Kurdish anti-government groups. Turkish philanthropist and human rights activist Osman Kavala, who was charged with espionage and attempting to overthrow the constitutional order, remains in prison.

Most recently, espionage charges have been brought against the former Istanbul mayor and Erdogan's political competitor, Ekrem Imamoglu, and a number of journalists.

Hakki Tas, a research fellow and expert on Turkey at the German Institute for Global and Area Studies, said the number of such cases have been increasing over the past few years.

Sources indicate that on the one hand, Turkey has the right to protect itself from foreign intelligence services — especially given geopolitical competition and conflict in the region, he argued. On the other hand, there's a long tradition of bringing the Turkish opposition to court to face security charges.

"What foreigners or employees of foreign institutions have experienced in recent years is a continuation of this pattern," Tas told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, media outlets and NGOs critical of the government have faced investigations, trials and other sorts of state sanctions for years. The ruling AKP party has also brought in its own version of a so-called "foreign agent law.".

These sorts of espionage cases serve both a domestic and foreign policy function, Tas stated.

Sources indicate that for locals, "contact with a foreign institution, foreign funding or even a perfectly normal salary could become part of an investigation someday," he explained. "For opposition figures and civil society organizations, in particular, this can become a security issue.".

In terms of foreign policy, the cases also show other countries that there are limits to their activities inside Turkey. These kinds of accusations seem to become more frequent when there's some sort of foreign policy tension — for example, after Western criticism of how opposition groups were dealt with after the alleged coup in 2016, the aforementioned disputes about arms deliveries in connection with Syria, or criticism from abroad about the removal of elected mayors in Turkey.

It can also serve as a kind of "hostage diplomacy," Tas said.

The case of US pastor Brunson is a good example. After his arrest, the Turkish government proposed a trade with the Americans. They wanted to exchange Turkish preacher Fethullah Gulen, who lived in the US and who the Turkish government blamed for the 2016 coup attempt.

This suspicion of foreign institutions isn't something that the Erdogan government invented, Tas points out. In the early 2000s, several representatives of German organizations were already made to stand trial in Turkey. At the time, it was alleged that, among other things, the German spy service was using German foundations as a front for conspiracy.

Industry observers note that in some of the best-known cases, defendants often don't end up convicted of espionage. In the case of activist Osman Kavala, he was initially acquitted of espionage several times and spent two years in prison, just because of those charges.

Sources indicate that but Tas remarked that's no surprise, referring to a 1979 work about the sociology of law written by US law professor Malcolm Feeley. It's title: "The Process Is the Punishment.".

Who did figure 3? Why scientists should make experimental contributions visible

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (930 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Highlighting who was responsible for each experiment could be a boost to many researchers’ careers.Credit: miniseries/Getty.
  • In a recent development, I ask this question surprisingly often when reading the literature.
  • After years of working in experimental cell biology, collaborating with other laboratories, reviewing papers and handling manuscripts as an editor, I have come to recognize that this is more than an inconvenience.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Highlighting who was responsible for each experiment could be a boost to many researchers’ careers.Credit: miniseries/Getty.

In a recent development, I ask this question surprisingly often when reading the literature. I might be interested in a particular imaging approach, trying to understand an experiment in detail when reviewing a manuscript or simply want to contact a study author who has experience with a technique. I look at the author list, then the contribution statement, and reach the same conclusion: I have no idea who did the work.

After years of working in experimental cell biology, collaborating with other laboratories, reviewing papers and handling manuscripts as an editor, I have come to recognize that this is more than an inconvenience. By obscuring who does what in a research project, we are losing an crucial piece of information about how science is done — and the people who do it.

Digital badges aim to clear up politics of authorship.

Digital badges aim to clear up politics of authorship.

In a recent development, this has become particularly obvious to me as my research has become more collaborative. My projects can involve advanced microscopy, molecular biology, animal experiments and computational analysis, each performed by a different group. This is one of the things I enjoy most about modern science: collaborations allow us to answer questions that none of us could address alone. But they also make individual expertise increasingly difficult to see.

When I started in research 20 years ago, papers generally had fewer authors and the experimental work was performed in one or two laboratories. Today, papers routinely have 10, 20 or more authors, with projects spread across several institutes. A 2024 study1 in Scientometrics found that the mean number of authors on papers in the PubMed database grew by more than 50% between 2000 and 2020 (from 3.99 to 6.25). Author-contribution statements help to delineate individual roles in a project, but only to a point. If five people are listed under investigation, three under methodology and four under analysis, I still cannot tell who performed any one experiment.

Anyone who has spent time at the bench knows that experiments require more than simply following the methods section of a paper.

I have seen young researchers spend months, sometimes years, developing expertise in a technique. When the resulting study is published through a large collaboration, that researcher might become one name among many, credited with investigation or methodology. But those words do not tell the person reading the paper that this is the scientist who knows how this experiment works.

Sources indicate that for early-career researchers, that’s a missed opportunity. Publications are not only records of scientific findings, they also demonstrate technical proficiency. Being able to say, “I am an author on this paper”, is valuable. Being identifiable as the person who generated a particular piece of evidence provides a different and, in some circumstances, more useful form of recognition.

According to recent reports, and there’s another benefit. As a reviewer and editor, I sometimes have technical questions. The corresponding author is, appropriately, my point of contact. But they might not be the person who performed or directly supervised the experiment I care about and, over time, they might not remember who did. PhD students graduate, postdocs change institutions and collaborations evolve. Five years after publication, identifying the person who remembers exactly how an experiment was performed can be difficult.

We rightly devote enormous attention to reproducibility. We record catalogue numbers for antibodies, identify instruments and software versions and deposit raw data sets. Yet we often fail to record something much simpler: who generated the data. I am not suggesting this as a way of assigning blame when something goes wrong — authorship implies collective responsibility for a published study. I see it instead as a strategy to provide traceability of expertise.

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

Sources indicate that but this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund.

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors.

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Recent findings suggest that despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta stated: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'.

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an glitch which Arteta must urgently address.

It is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

Sources indicate that he obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

One back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners.

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund revealed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

Sources indicate that after the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more quickly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund joked that there is ‘only one club in Manchester’ after netting against Manchester City in Napoli’s 2-2 Champions League draw at The Etihad on Tuesday evening, but his comments were not well received by pundits on CBS, who criticised the Dane for his ‘poor timing’: ‘He’s playing for Napoli, who by the way are in absolute shambles’.

Recent findings suggest that hojlund opened the scoring on his return to Manchester in an eventual 2-2 draw away against the Premier League heavyweights on Tuesday evening. Napoli were widely praised by the Italian press for their performance on the night, and despite coming into the tie as underdogs, Napoli were just a few minutes away from holding out for the full three points.

Hojlund joked after full-time that there is ‘only one club in Manchester’, nodding back to his time with Manchester United.

“I was really happy for my goal, the fans were jeering me, so I was saying there’s only one club in Manchester,” said the former United striker in his post-match interview after full-time.

Those comments did not go down well with pundits in the CBS Studio, who criticised the Dane for his lack of judgement.

“He’s playing for Napoli, who by the way are in absolute shambles,” mentioned Mike Grella after watching Hojlund’s post-match interview.

“Second year on the turn they might not qualify for the knock-out stages. They did not win the game tonight. 36 teams, 24 go through, 12 of them get eliminated. There’s that.

“You’re also wearing the Napoli badge, they’re paying your stub at the moment and you’re talking about the time you spent at Manchester United, which, by the way, was another shambolic moment for you and Manchester United.

“Look, I think he’s trying to be harmless and funny with that, but man, really poor timing and really not reading the room.”.

Troy Deeney added: “Irrelevant of all of that, they got rid of you. They got rid of you because you’re not good enough. You’re at a massive club. You’re not playing for Mickey Mouse FC down the road, you’re playing for Napoli, a huge club with history.

You’ve not only infuriated the rest of us, you’ve infuriated Napoli fans, who are now gonna go this weekend, after you’ve come out and questioned the manager’s tactics last time out in the Champions League and now you’re saying that’s your club, off you pop mate.”.

There has also been criticism of the criticism.

Some on social media labelled the comments from the CBS pundits as ‘stupid’. “Troy Deeney, the greatest sportsman who never played for Man Utd or Napoli. Never got close to them either. Don’t even know who the others are,” wrote one supporter on X.

Recent findings suggest that “Done nothing wrong! Can’t question his commitment to Napoli! They have had a drop off this season but he generally has been a very good servant to Napoli regardless of his personal football allegiances,” another added.

Recent findings suggest that one Manchester United supporter commented: “Chill out lads, he’s a long time United fan scoring against a rival. He didn’t mean “that’s my club right now” and have you got any other languages between you?? How’s your Danish?”.

Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.
  • In a recent development, these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday.
  • Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he indicates little sign of putting down his guitar.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

He mocks Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the Palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "Lady Liberty." It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

In a recent development, these themes run throughout Wolf Biermann's new album "Unterm Haar nur Himmel" ("Beneath Hair, Only Sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Biermann remains one of Germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he indicates little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the complications shaping the world today.

Sources indicate that in his recent song "Moritat von den Liebespaaren" ("Ballad of the Lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

Sources indicate that this outspokenness was instilled in Biermann early on. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish.

Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Just a few months later, British and American bombers attacked Hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly said in interviews. When the sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. The house above them was burning.

It has been revealed that yet Biermann has noted his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. We searched for a way out. [...] Death was everywhere. 40,000 people died. They had no chance. But I did. My strong mama.".

Biermann's mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann once recalled. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. I was supposed to build communism.".

In 1953, while countless people were fleeing East Germany, Biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. He was just 16 at the time. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble, and also began writing and performing his political songs.

In a recent development, biermann soon realized that life in East Germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann said. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer.".

In a recent development, in 1965, East Germany's ruling Socialist Unity Party, the SED, imposed a blanket ban on Biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Yet, to his great surprise, the East German authorities allowed him to travel to Cologne, West Germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

Sources indicate that on November 16, while still on tour in West Germany, Biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the German Democratic Republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. ".

Industry observers note that I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

In a petition, leading East German intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

"The SED leadership expected an angry media response from the West. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann wrote.

Afterward, Biermann sank into a deep depression. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he said.

In a recent development, he became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he stated. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom.".

According to recent reports, the singer-songwriter plans to spend his 90th birthday at home in Hamburg with his wife and manager, Pamela. For the first time in his life, he stated, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children.

"I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency.

It has been revealed that and should he ever die, he said, he wants to be buried at Berlin's cemetery where some renowned German writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them Bertolt Brecht, Anna Seghers and Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.

This article was originally written in German.

While there can be little doubt about Unai Emery’s status as an elite manager in the modern game, matches at the Nou Camp continue to be the stuff of nightmares.

His record at Barcelona now reads 15 defeats from 16 matches and this was another difficult evening with Aston Villa unable to banish the demons for the man who has transformed their club.

According to recent reports, it was Emery’s 55th birthday and with the Prince of Wales and Prince George both in attendance, Villa fans were hopeful of another memorable European night. But from the moment midfielder João Gomes handed Barcelona their opening goal, it was always going to be an uphill struggle.

Emery has suffered many uncomfortable occasions at this grand old stadium, none more so than the notorious “La Remontada” of 2017 when he last competed here in the Champions League with Paris St-Germain.

This latest visit would become his heaviest defeat in Europe as Villa manager. With three wins from the opening four matches, they still have a fine chance of progressing to the knockout stage. Yet, aside from the mistakes, there will be a sense that Villa could have capitalised more against a team in the midst of a defensive injury crisis. They did have a number of chances in the first half but were left to rue their lack of ruthlessness.
