According to recent reports, aston Villa have made the trip over to Spain to take on Barcelona in the Champions League on matchday four. These teams last met all the way back in 1983, when they met in the European Super Cup. Barcelona won the first leg 1-0 at home before Aston Villa claimed a 3-0 victory at Villa Park, meaning Villa progressed 3-1 on aggregate.

Aston Villa have made the perfect start to their Champions League campaign, winning all three games, beating Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking, scoring 12 goals in the process. Unai Emery’s side drew 1-1 at home against Fulham in the league on Saturday. Emery, who celebrates his 55th birthday today, has a very dismal record against Barcelona, taking just three wins from 30 matches. His last Champions League game at the Nou Camp was infamous as his PSG side lost 6-1 to go out in the last 16 back in 2017 despite winning the first leg of that tie 4-0.

Recent findings suggest that “In 1982, Villa won the European Cup, and we like to think about playing in this competition again and trying to repeat that success,” Emery said. “Barcelona are favourites for what they have done in the last ten years; now they need to prove why they are favourites.

“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”.

It has been revealed that barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick noted. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which demonstrated it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”.

Chelsea have reportedly held transfer talks with Bournemouth over a January deal for Alex Scott, with things heading in a ‘positive’ direction.

That’s according to a report from Simon Phillips, with the Chelsea insider providing some interesting details on his Substack this morning.

Scott has long been strongly linked with Chelsea, and it seems things are moving in the right direction in terms of the Blues bringing the England international to Stamford Bridge in the middle of the season.

“I have had it confirmed by my top SPTC Source that Chelsea and Bournemouth did once again hold more talks around Alex Scott to Chelsea in January, over the international break. And this source describes the talks as ‘positive’,” Phillips wrote.

“Remember, another top SPTC Source told us about these talks, and that as a result of them, Chelsea are Bournemouth had actually got pretty close on a fee now – there is some work to do on add-ons and structuring of any deal.

“However, our top source also notes more clubs have started to sniff around for Scott now as well, even though he has verbally agreed to Chelsea’s terms. Nothing is done yet, it’s key to keep reiterating this.”.

Scott has shown himself to be a superb talent during his time at Bournemouth, and it seems inevitable that he’ll eventually end up moving to a bigger club.

The Cherries have done well to cash in on some star players for a profit in recent times, such as Antoine Semenyo, Dean Huijsen, and Milos Kerkez.

We’ve previously reported here on Chelsea pursuing Scott, with Bournemouth open to a sale and other clubs also mentioned as suitors.

Sky Sports have linked Arsenal with an interest in the 23-year-old, while you can also see below for Ben Jacobs posting on X about Liverpool also potentially being in the race for his signature….

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday.

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal.

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

It has been revealed that 'Yeah, it's good banter,' he said on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'.

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

It has been revealed that he would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

In a recent development, it was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'.

Francesco Camarda is the latest Milan player to be ruled out of Milan’s upcoming Europa League clash against Olympiacos after picking up an ankle problem in training according to Wednesday’s reports.

Milan are due to take on Olympiacos in Athens on Thursday evening and will have to do so without eight of their first-team players.

Luka Modric is expected to be unavailable with a muscular issue, as are Strahinja Pavlovic, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Alexis Saelemaekers and Ruben Loftus-Cheek.

Camarda is the latest player to be added to the Milan injury list after suffering an ankle issue and is unlikely to be called up for the Olympiacos clash as a result.

The Rossoneri are in for a tough test away against the Greek side on Thursday night: The hosts are in sixth place ahead of kick-off and remain unbeaten after their first four matches in the competition, with three wins and one draw totalling 10 points.

Milan, meanwhile, are presently outside of the knock-out round qualification spots, all the way down in 28th place after one win and three defeats, against Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, from their first four matches.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Kyiv would withdraw from its eastern region of ‌Donbas ⁠in exchange ⁠for joining NATO, according to remarks to the media published on Saturday.

The suggestion was made following the latest round of peace talks in Abu Dhabi to bring Russia's nearly 5-year war in Ukraine to a close.

Recent findings suggest that the Ukrainian leader told reporters: "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would ⁠Ukraine ​withdraw from Donbas?'".

Zelenskyy repeated Kyiv's position that it was not willing to cede territory to Russia. But he added that if the country reached a comprehensive deal, including security guarantees, a ‌strong ​and well-funded Ukrainian army and funds to rebuild, he would put the question ​to the public in a referendum.

"That ​is why ⁠I believe NATO is back on the ⁠agenda. ​But you have also heard [Russian President Vladimir] Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation.".

Zelenskyy said the prospect of NATO membership in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas has not been raised before.

He also warned about Moscow's plan to  change the continent's security architecture, saying it could lead to more conflict.

Putin has demanded that NATO pull back its troops from the Russian border, which European Union leaders have strongly criticized.

"This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations," Zelenskyy added.

"Real security in Europe means the EU and NATO. That's it. There is no other security in Europe.".

Manchester United chiefs have conceded that they must back new manager Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window given how their season is currently panning out.

Hopes were high that Man United were going to push on following the permanent appointment of Michael Carrick in the summer, after a stunning run of form under the 45-year-old's leadership in the first half of 2026 saw them secure a third-place finish in the Premier League, and a return to Champions League football as a result.

It would be no exaggeration to say the 2026-27 campaign to date has been a disaster though, with Pochettino replacing Carrick in the Old Trafford dugout following the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa prior to the international break.

United went into Sunday's clash against Liverpool in 19th position in the Premier League table, having won just one of their top flight fixtures this term, at home to newly-promoted Ipswich Town.

Fans would have been hoping for a fresh manager bounce under the Argentine, but the chances of that happening were ultimately extinguished following Leny Yoro's eighth minute red card, which has since been overturned.

That decision doesn't help United though, given they were beaten 4-0 on the day, which has left them in dire straits in terms of their Premier League position.

The Red Devils have won two of their four matches in the Champions League though, and they have the opportunity to give themselves a confidence booster ahead of a big league game against Brentford at Old Trafford this weekend when they travel to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night.

Pochettino has another five weeks working with this squad before he has the chance to add new faces to the squad, with the Times reporting that, despite their defensive issues this term, a striker will be the main priority.

Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been linked, while TEAMtalk claim that intermediaries have been in touch with United over the potential availability of Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney.

The 30-year-old has been in outstanding goalscoring form in Saudi Arabia after making the move from Brentford, but is stated to be open to a return to European football in 2027.

The report adds that a switch to Old Trafford would strongly appeal to the England international.

We all know that Harry Kane was arguably at his best in a Tottenham shirt when Pochettino was manager there, and the Ballon d'Or winner cannot speak highly enough of the Argentine following their time together.

Kane has just signed a latest contract at Bayern Munich and is currently injured, and there is no chance, in the short-term at least, that he will be returning to the Premier League.

In the absence of the injured Benjamin Sesko, Pochettino would love to find a striker as close to Kane as possible, but that is never going to be easy in a January window.

But if the 54-year-old head coach wants a talismanic centre-forward with Premier League experience and a prolific goal record, there won't be too many better options than Toney.

The 30-year-old played a starring role for Brentford in the English top flight before making the switch to Saudi Arabia, where he has produced some ridiculous goal numbers.

His displays led to him being described as 'one of the best strikers in the world' by former Al-Ahli sporting director Rui Pedro, which reveals how highly he is rated, and the quality he has in front of goal.

If the deal is right in January and Toney is ready to join, he could be a no-brainer addition for a club looking to turn their fortunes around.

Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1273 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it was 5:55 a.m.
  • Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • Sources indicate that reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Sources indicate that reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government plans to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

But here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that but that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

It has been revealed that if the new debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

This development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

Sources indicate that to understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social issues, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding latest investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

What's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

It has been revealed that the rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are plans for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

Sources indicate that the pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

Sources indicate that the Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

According to recent reports, anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on latest debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

Sources indicate that the key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

This would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Sources indicate that this also means that interest rates on newly introduced loans are not set as high. This is an key point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

Sources indicate that at the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

Industry observers note that the prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

#118173. Breaking: Menopause can speed up brain ageing — hormone therapy might protect it

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1015 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Menopause can speed up brain ageing — hormone therapy might protect it

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1015 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hormonal changes during menopause could explain why Alzheimer’s disease affects more women than men.
  • Some types of hormone therapy for menopause are linked to better memory performance and a reduced risk of mild cognitive impairment, according to data presented at a neuroscience conference that began on 14 November.
  • The research is part of a series of studies presented at the Society for Neuroscience’s Neuroscience 2026 conference that reveal differences in cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression on the basis of biological sex or life stage.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hormonal changes during menopause could explain why Alzheimer’s disease affects more women than men. Credit: Maskot/Getty.

Some types of hormone therapy for menopause are linked to better memory performance and a reduced risk of mild cognitive impairment, according to data presented at a neuroscience conference that began on 14 November. The findings suggest that some therapies could be protective against the brain changes that often precede Alzheimer’s disease, say the authors, although more research is needed to confirm this effect.

The research is part of a series of studies presented at the Society for Neuroscience’s Neuroscience 2026 conference that reveal differences in cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression on the basis of biological sex or life stage. The studies have not been peer reviewed.

According to recent reports, women are twice as likely to develop AD than are men. But the reasons for these sex differences are poorly understood and poorly studied, say researchers in the field. “The women’s health gap is huge,” Liisa Galea, a neuroscientist at the University of Toronto in Canada, told reporters at the conference, which was held in Washington DC. Part of the problem is that studies often do not analyse sex differences, she adds.

Sources indicate that researchers think that hormonal changes that happen during menopause could partly explain why the disease affects women and men differently. For instance, going through menopause early, between 40 and 45 years old, is thought to increase a woman’s risk of cognitive decline and developing AD. Some studies have found that oestrogen — which decreases during menopause — has a protective effect on the brain.

Mateja Perović, a neuroscientist at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto, and her team wanted to know whether menopausal hormone therapy (MHT), which is used to supplement oestrogen levels and treat symptoms of menopause, can slow cognitive ageing and reduce the risk of developing AD. Perović indicates that previous studies have showed mixed results, but these studies had not differentiated between the different types of MHT1.

In a recent development, the team analysed the cognitive function of around 14,000 women who received different types of MHT or none at all2. They also compared cognitive function between women using MHT who had a genetic risk of developing AD and those who didn’t.

According to recent reports, they found that oestradiol-based treatments — which contain a compound that is chemically identical to the oestrogen produced by the body — were associated with better episodic memory in women without cognitive impairment than were treatments containing a mix of natural and synthetic oestrogens. Episodic memory refers to the ability to learn and recall information. A deficit in this can be an early symptom of AD. Women who did not receive any MHT also indicated better episodic memory than did those who received the mixed-oestrogen treatments.

Oestradiol-based MHT also indicated benefits for women who were not genetically predisposed to AD and had mild cognitive impairment, whereas the mixed-oestrogen MHT did not.

In a recent development, both treatment types were beneficial for other types of long-term memory function compared with no MHT for women who had mild cognitive impairment and carried a gene called APOE4, which is linked to an increased risk of developing AD. But MHT use did not affect the risk of progressing to dementia, suggesting that the treatments might improve a person’s cognitive function without preventing the disease.

In a recent development, when the researchers looked at structural brain changes using imaging techniques, they found that women with the APOE4 gene who took oestradiol had higher cortical thickness and less white-matter damage than did women not receiving MHT. Decreased cortical thickness, caused by the loss of neurons, is associated with decreased brain function and can be an early indicator of cognitive impairment. The findings suggest that oestradiol-based MHT might be particularly beneficial for women at higher risk of developing AD, claims Perović.

Mia Schaumberg, who studies healthy brain ageing at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Sippy Downs, Australia, claims it is promising that research is considering individual risk factors, such as genetics and differences in MHT composition, when looking at women’s cognitive health. “It is starting to gain the attention that it deserves,” she adds.

However, Susan Davis, an endocrinologist and researcher at Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, says that the effect of MHT on AD risk needs to be investigated in a randomized clinical trial to validate the findings of this study.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, although considered one of the hardest players in Premier League history, Vinnie Jones still divides opinion.
  • In a recent development, his era was the 1980s and '90s.
  • Sources indicate that as far as he was concerned, he only had one rival in the game when it came to being a hard man.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, although considered one of the hardest players in Premier League history, Vinnie Jones still divides opinion. This is where the distinction comes in between being a tough player and being a dirty one. Jones certainly had no qualms blowing his own trumpet and describing himself as a hard man.

In a recent development, his era was the 1980s and '90s. Although major changes in the game took place in that - for example, giving a red card for a professional foul - refereeing was generally more lenient. You could happily scythe opponents down and not always be immediately carded. More often than not, this is what Jones did.

Sources indicate that as far as he was concerned, he only had one rival in the game when it came to being a hard man. That was Liverpool's Steve McMahon. The two faced each other in the 1988 FA Cup Final. In that final, Wimbledon upset the odds, beating Liverpool 1-0. That remains one of the biggest shocks in football.

Jones had targeted McMahon in the cup final and got the opportunity to make his mark in the opening moments. The resulting tackle is one of the most famous in England's showpiece game. It was brutal too, but did not result in any cards. In a conversation with talkSPORT, Jones explained his thinking prior to the big game: “I’d watched a video and [Alan] Hansen or someone would knock the ball to [McMahon] who'd then let it come across him to open up so he could play it out the other side.

"The boys knew I was going to smash him because I’d told them that if I could early enough, the referee wasn’t going to send me off in front of in front of about 100,000 people, but I didn’t get too much of a response from the lads, so it was a bit of a gamble.".

This exact scenario played out in the opening moments of the cup final. True to form, McMahon received the ball just as Jones had envisaged he would. There was no time to hesitate. This was an opportunity for Jones to lay down a serious message to Liverpool.

"So when the ball came into him, I started running. I was about 30 yards away and I kept thinking, 'just open up', and he did and I thought, 'Merry Christmas'. BOOM!”.

Per the Liverpool Echo, Jones would later claim McMahon was his 'only real rival' in modern-day football for the accolade of 'hardest man in football'.

Jones vs McMahon Disciplinary Record (Club and Country).

Sources indicate that such was the time, there were no histrionics from McMahon. He simply got to his feet. McMahon plays down any belief that Jones's tackle was the catalyst that enabled Wimbledon to believe they could win the game. He asserted:.

Recent findings suggest that “It has nothing to do with the fact that Vinnie Jones made a neck-high tackle on me in the first five minutes of the final. I got up and got on with the game; that tackle didn’t worry me in the least. I’m sure he thought it upset me, but I can assure him that it didn’t.".

In a recent development, jones would later acknowledge that McMahon got his revenge in the end. Indeed, the Liverpool ace connected with Jones so forcefully with his studs, the Wales international was left needing stitches on a major cut.

Klinsmann: ‘Inter have to be very careful against Stuttgart, Esposito a step ahead of Tresoldi’

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jurgen Klinsmann has warned that Inter will need a strong defensive performance against VfB Stuttgart in the Champions League on Wednesday evening and feels that Pio Esposito is at the moment a ‘step ahead’ of Nicolo Tresoldi, who remains eligible to represent both Italy and Germany at international level.
  • Klinsmann spoke in-depth to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of Inter’s Champions League clash against Stuttgart on Wednesday evening, discussing the ‘superior’ squad that Cristian Chivu has, the quality of his centre-forwards and the pending decision that Tresoldi has to make over his international future.
  • Inter are heading into their Champions League game against Stuttgart off the back of a 4-4 draw against Atalanta.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jurgen Klinsmann has warned that Inter will need a strong defensive performance against VfB Stuttgart in the Champions League on Wednesday evening and feels that Pio Esposito is at the moment a ‘step ahead’ of Nicolo Tresoldi, who remains eligible to represent both Italy and Germany at international level.

Klinsmann spoke in-depth to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of Inter’s Champions League clash against Stuttgart on Wednesday evening, discussing the ‘superior’ squad that Cristian Chivu has, the quality of his centre-forwards and the pending decision that Tresoldi has to make over his international future.

Inter are heading into their Champions League game against Stuttgart off the back of a 4-4 draw against Atalanta. The Nerazzurri had led 3-1 midway through the second half, but a particularly poor end to the game saw them drop two crucial points in Serie A.

“Unfortunately I only saw the last half hour, the bad part,” Klinsmann told La Gazzetta dello Sport.

“Inter always score a lot of goals, but sometimes they suffer a bit too much. But I wouldn’t worry, everybody knows the team’s value and they’re well aware of it in Germany as well.

It has been revealed that “They’re normal mistakes. When you play a more attacking game, like this year, you also risk conceding more goals. Every game is also different from the last, and it’s always difficult in Bergamo. It was in Inter’s hands, but it slipped away once they felt that they’d already won. Atalanta were also underestimated, it’s still the team that amazed all of Europe.”.

It has been revealed that asked for his assessment of Chivu as a head coach, Klinsmann stated: “He’s created a fluid team. He has a system that suits the players’ characteristics, the 3-5-2. And then, obviously, I’m crazy about Pio Esposito, who always puts on a show.

“Now Chivu has three heavyweights in attack. As well as Pio, Thuram has also refound his rhythm, and after his injury, Lautaro will return to the level we all know of him.

“It’s only November. The team has to still be in the running when it gets to the spring and everything is going at 200 miles per hour. As for the league, they shouldn’t look at the standings. Gattuso has Lazio’s enthusiasm, Gasperini is making Roma fly, but nobody has Inter’s squad.”.

Klinsmann was asked whether it could be a ‘problem’ later down the line to have three strikers who all deserve to start, when only two spots are available in the XI.

Recent findings suggest that “As long as you’re playing in all competitions, especially the Champions League, it’s fine to have three exceptional players and do some rotations,” he replied. “Given the number of matches, you can’t just have one starting pair to rely on.

“There is a bit of a risk to the group’s spirit, though, because all three are rightly ambitious and always want to play. And who do you leave out? Marcus has unique characteristics, Lautaro is the face of Inter and Pio makes Italy smile.”.

Speaking of Italy, Tresoldi has still not yet decided which nation he will represent at senior international level. The Club Brugge talent was born in Cagliari but moved to Germany as a teenager and is a regular for the Germany U21 squad. He is also eligible for Argentina.

Klinsmann indicates that he doesn’t know which way Tresoldi will turn either way, but he does not think it will be a major glitch if he does not select Italy, given Esposito’s talents.

“At the moment, Pio is a step ahead of Tresoldi, who is, however, still an enormous talent. We’ll see if he can make the step up in the coming months, but I really think he can.

“It would be great to have him for either nation, for us and for you, but certain decisions, made with the heart, have to be respected.”.

Klinsmann was also asked whether he sees any of his own playing qualities in any of Inter’s three first-choice strikers.

Recent findings suggest that “At a glance, I wouldn’t say any of them. To me, Pio reminds me of Aldo Serena: He’s always in the right place, he’s strong and intelligent, both protecting the ball and scoring. I was more about finding the space. I ran a lot, I could go to the left or the right. Maybe I’m a bit more of a Thuram.”.

Previewing Inter’s upcoming opponents, Stuttgart, Klinsmann remarked: “Stuttgart have returned to their previous level in recent years under Seb Hoeness. They won’t win the league every year given that there’s Bayern Munich, but they do have to compete at the top.

“As a club, they’re much more stable today than they were 10 years ago. They play beautiful, entertaining football in a stadium that was renovated for the last EUROs and it’s a little gem. Always sold out, 60,000 people. Stuttgart are all about the fans, you’ll see it in San Siro, those fans marching to the stadium before the match is a show within the show.”.

He also pointed to a few players to watch out for: “Undav and Demirovic can punish you. Out wide, Fuhrich somewhat resembles my old friend Alessandro Bianchi: You never know which way he’ll go. He always knows how to be dangerous and always gets a lot of assists.

Industry observers note that “As a squad, Inter are superior, but be careful: If Stuttgart catch you on the counter, you might struggle to fix it and turn the game around. INter might be the favourites, but they have to be very, very careful in defence.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

According to recent reports, “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found matter had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Sources indicate that liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

But even Kuyt would have been the first to recognise the helping hand Fenerbahce were afforded. Liverpool were meek, naïve, and while the Turkish side danced in the rain on the Asian side of the city, Iraola was left to dissect the most chastening 90 minutes of his short Anfield career.

“It’s frustration because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play,” said Iraola. “During most of the game, we were thinking: ‘OK we can win this one.’ But obviously it hasn’t happened. We conceded, I think, messy goals, especially the first and the third one. The second one is a rebound.”.

Recent findings suggest that yet it all started so smoothly. For all that Fenerbahce tried to put Liverpool out of their stride with a soundtrack of high-pitched whistling, Iraola’s side kept the ball well and they might have been ahead in the fifth minute but Victor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola, playing as a central striker, erred.

According to recent reports, another chance went begging when Joe Gomez fizzed a ball across the six-yard box that was screaming to be converted, but nobody could apply the finishing touch. When Trey Nyoni put Liverpool ahead, it seemed like all those local predictions of a resounding away win would come true.

What a moment for Trey Nyoni 🥹 The young Liverpool midfielder scores his first professional goal, and he does it on the Champions League stage ✨ 📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Vtj4Yd3tnn.

Nyoni is a terrific player-in-the-making and the joy of seeing him wheel away, having become Liverpool’s second youngest Champions League scorer behind Trent Alexander-Arnold, was everything you want to see in football.

So for the landscape to change so dramatically – and so swiftly – after Liverpool had taken the lead was staggering, and it all came about after Irfan Can Kahveci slid in and turned a cross from Mattéo Guendouzi on to the bar.

Those who remember Kuyt from his Anfield days 15 years ago will recall a player who never considered any cause to be lost and the Dutchman implored his team to attack the flanks with pace, even earning himself a yellow card at one point. Eventually, the pressure paid off.

Greenwood had felt aggrieved not to have been given a 23rd-minute penalty, after Kostas Tsimikas placed his hands on his back, but he did not have to wait long to make an impact, his opportunity coming after Dominik Szoboszlai conceded a cheap free-kick.

Szoboszlai is rapidly becoming an enigma. How can a player with the gift of being able to score goals from the heavens make the mistakes of a weekend amateur? There was no need for him to foul N’Golo Kanté but the error was compounded, Greenwood’s strike deflecting off Jérémy Jacquet.

Recent findings suggest that since Manchester United felt duty-bound to sell Greenwood in 2024 the former England forward has continued his career away from the Premier League. After leaving Marseille he has found a home in Istanbul where the fans have taken to him and they bellowed his name following the equaliser.

Alisson Becker, wrong-footed by Jacquet’s decision to break off from the wall and turn his body, was livid and rightly so. Liverpool had gone from sublime (in patches) to ridiculous and the passage of play up to the interval was hugely uncomfortable.

Sources indicate that would things settle down after the break? Not a bit of it. Liverpool, worryingly for Iraola, could not stamp any authority and though there was a brief respite when Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak combined after being introduced as substitutes, the lead felt as sustainable as a snowball in a sauna.

Recent findings suggest that A draw would have been fine but Liverpool contrived to throw it away completely. Alisson stayed stuck on his line as a high ball came in, Nyoni, Jacquet and Alexis Mac Allister were weak in the challenge and Muriqi nodded in to spark pandemonium.

Having conceded three against LASK Linz and then another two in a dreadful 45 minutes against Villarreal before shipping another three here, Liverpool have shown that, as things stand, they cannot be considered as serious players in this competition. How can they be with defending so bad?

“We put ourselves in a good position,” Isak told LFC TV afterwards. “To lose this game is not a chaos situation, we just have to get back to winning games. If we win our next game then we are back to a really good position.”.

Isak is right but the “if” is suddenly a massive one – it will remain that way unless Liverpool learn quickly.

Manchester United are leaning towards allowing Lisandro Martinez to leave the club next summer despite already lacking depth at the centre-back position. United are in troubled times, right now sat in 19th position and desperately hoping new boss Mauricio Pochettino can turn things around quickly.

Liverpool thrashed United 4-0 in Pochettino's first game, although the Red Devils were not helped by a red card awarded to Leny Yoro that was later removed on appeal. But United did not play well in any case, and they certainly didn't defend well amid ongoing issues at the back.

According to recent reports, matthijs de Ligt lacks match fitness and sharpness, while Yoro is still learning and Martinez has been in poor form this season. Harry Maguire, meanwhile, cannot get a look in.

Industry observers note that united have some interesting contract decisions to make in the summer window, and one of the biggest is Martinez, who initially arrived at the club on a £56.7million deal. Two long-term ACL injuries have followed, and it's fair to say the Argentine hasn't lived up to expectations. He didn't help himself when he spoke out against the club earlier this summer amid struggles under Michael Carrick.

Martinez is out of contract in the summer, but United do have an option to extend the deal by one year, albeit they are only likely to activate that if both they and the player want to continue their relationship.

According to recent reports, and according to GIVEMESPORT's Ben Jacobs, United are not likely to extend the deal as things stand. He remarked on the Market Madness podcast: “I think the Lisandro Martinez direction of travel is a departure, and there is the option to extend by one year. But my gut notes that Manchester United, even if they can’t get defenders in the winter, will add further in the summer because they don’t just need one defender; they need a centre-back, they need a left-back, you could say they need a right-back.

According to recent reports, "And in getting these full-backs, they might even get a full-back that’s a centre-back. So you might have centre-back, a wing-back that can play centre-back, and you’ve obviously still got young players like Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro.

So this feels to me like Martinez, on form and on age, and even to a degree on wage, although he’s not like top five at Manchester United, the beginning of the end.

"And even if Man United extend the contract, that might just be a protection so they can still sell him.”.

In a recent development, there have been reports that Pochettino wants to keep Martinez, with the defender certainly having the ability with the ball at his feet that the newly introduced United boss likes in his centre-backs, and there is an obvious Argentine connection. But there is also a business reality to the contract situation, and that will mean club higher ups like Jacon Wilcox will get a major say.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026.

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United plan to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go major in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget….

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause.

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap.

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford.

Recent findings suggest that signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

In a recent development, collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City.

Sources indicate that united made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

It has been revealed that rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace.

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

In a recent development, mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

Sources indicate that for all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and major clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace.

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham.

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

It has been revealed that in the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Industry observers note that richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached.

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan.

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

It has been revealed that the England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack.

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart.

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – vital given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back.

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid.

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it.

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future.

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco.

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ mentioned Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’.

Pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

#118166. How AI is likely to change Germany's job market

How AI is likely to change Germany's job market

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?
  • Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.
  • Industry observers note that "I've always been a bit cautious about this issue in recent years," he mentioned, as reported by the news outlet RND.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the German government's 2026 Digital Summit in early November, Chancellor Friedrich Merz was asked by a journalist to square a difficult economic circle: If artificial intelligence could make hundreds of thousands of people redundant in the next few years, might it become necessary for the government to give people a basic income to ease the ensuing economic disaster?

Surprisingly, Merz didn't respond with a flat dismissal — as might be expected from a conservative politician known for his neoliberal, market-friendly views.

Industry observers note that "I've always been a bit cautious about this issue in recent years," he mentioned, as reported by the news outlet RND. "However, I'm also well aware that the issue of AI will change our working world so fundamentally that we'll have to give serious thought to many of these issues in the coming years — including the question: Is our productivity not good enough?".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

What makes this ambiguity notable is that much of Merz's policies since becoming chancellor last year have involved making Germans work more: His government's planned pension reforms would see Germany's retirement age being raised. In July, he declared a crackdown on sick leave. And in spring 2025, having barely taken office, he caused much consternation by criticizing the concept of a "work-life balance" and declaring, "We in this country must work more and more efficiently.".

But those policies seem to contradict the impending realities of the labor market in an AI world.

This week, the head of Germany's Federal Employment Agency, Andrea Nahles, warned that the introduction AI would cost Germany as many 800,000 jobs in the next 15 years. Though she also remarked AI could eventually create a similar number of jobs, clearly the socioeconomic upheaval would be considerable.

Nahles is not the only leading figure concerned about job losses caused by AI. Karsten Wildberger, Germany's minister for digital transformation and government modernization, takes any opportunity he can to warn that Germany must prepare for the economic disruptions of AI.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

And even for Wildberger, a former CEO of a massive retail manufacturer, part of the future economy might come down to giving people free money. He was convinced, he told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung in March, "that an unconditional basic income can be part of the solution to cushion the upheavals in the labor market.".

Recent findings suggest that campaigners have cautiously welcomed this new openness from unexpected quarters. "It demonstrates that in the face of technological transformation we also need to look differently at the question of how we need to secure people's economic stability," mentioned Kirsten Herrmann, board member at the nonprofit Mein Grundeinkommen (My Basic Income), which runs various projects examining the social and economic impact of universal basic income (UBI).

"But I also think that individual statements by politicians don't amount to a political change, of course," she told DW. "It just means that we need to enter a serious and constructive debate about what kind of a role a basic income can play.".

According to recent reports, the idea of a universal basic income is very old: English Renaissance philosopher Thomas More mentions it in his 1516 book Utopia, for instance. But since the 20th century, it has largely been seen as an idealistic notion adopted by leftists — that is, until some of the world's most high-profile tech bosses latched onto the idea as a way to offset the utopian advances they said AI would bring.

In 2017, Elon Musk, who had co-founded the corporation OpenAI two years earlier, predicted that a universal basic income would at some stage become inevitable. Since then, leading figures in the AI sector, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the other founder of OpenAI, have all gone on record in support of UBI (though Altman's interest has cooled somewhat since he introduced a massive UBI experiment in the US in 2019).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, but Herrmann said it's a "double-edged sword" when such figures mention the idea. She isn't convinced that organizations like hers and people Elon Musk want the same thing.

In a recent development, "On the one hand, it's always nice when the debate about a basic income gets attention from prominent voices," she said. "On the other hand, the basic income that people from the tech business talk about is a kind of neoliberal basic income: They talk about what to do when there are no more profitable jobs for people, because they still actually do need people to do certain things, whereas we talk about a basic income that is meant to give people a secure economic base — before the crisis in the job market happens.".

What makes the comments of Merz and Wildberger all the more eyebrow-raising is that mainstream German economists have long since rejected the basic income idea.

Sources indicate that dominik Enste, director of the democracy, society, and economic ethics department at the German Economic Institute in Cologne, dismissed the idea out of hand — AI or no AI. UBI was, he said, just too expensive, especially in a country that already has plenty of social welfare costs.

"Many economists have calculated that implementing this in many countries is financially unfeasible — in Germany, for one, simply because of the need to fund commitments that have already been made (including pension payments)," he told DW in an email.

Recent findings suggest that however, he also added: "We will have to change our social security systems if work is replaced by AI and, if necessary, tax AI-generated income. But it will be a conditional basic income that still provides incentives to earn a living.".

In a recent development, other economists are more positive about the idea. "How this plays out depends on many choices we make, and on who makes these choices, in whose interest," said Maximilian Kasy, professor of economics at the University of Oxford and author of a book on the impact of AI on society. "But a lot of the current thrust is to replace workers to increase profits and increase corporate control, though this is not the only path possible.".

Kasy thinks a basic income could be a good solution, "especially if it's financed in a progressive way (so that only those at the lower end of the income distribution are net recipients)," he wrote. "The 'small print' matters very much, though!".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, if the warnings of Wildberger, Musk, Altman et al. are to be believed, AI is already causing a bigger upheaval than any other technological advance in history, partly because of the speed of the innovations, but also because of the scale of the potential impact.

Recent findings suggest that AI innovation is affecting the jobs of the traditional urban middle classes across the entire world. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund predicted that some 40% of employment in the world would be shaped by AI innovations, and as much as 60% in rich, industrialized nations.

For her part, Herrmann thinks we are not yet asking the truly fundamental questions about the socioeconomic implications of AI: Not just how do we replace the lost jobs and keep the capitalist system going, but what do we actually want to use AI for? As she put it: "Who actually profits when we become more productive through AI? And how do we redistribute that profit to everyone?".

This, she argued, is why there needs to be more debate about how exactly AI is used in the world of work. "Which jobs are going to be replaced by AI is not some law of nature," said Herrmann . "It's something that we can shape politically and socially — and then the bigger question is: Who gets a say?".

Arsenal are reportedly considering a surprise move for Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney as Mikel Arteta explores opportunities to strengthen his attack during the January transfer window.

The England international could return to the Premier League after leaving Brentford for Saudi Arabia in 2024, with several English clubs monitoring his situation.

Although Arsenal have invested heavily in their forward line, signing an experienced goalscorer could provide Arteta with another valuable attacking option during the second half of the season.

According to a report circulating on X, Arsenal are weighing up a potential move for Toney ahead of the winter transfer window.

While that particular claim remains unconfirmed, separate reporting suggests the Gunners are aware of the striker’s potential availability.

According to TEAMtalk, intermediaries have informed Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham about the possibility of signing Toney in January.

The 30-year-old has already scored 16 goals this season, demonstrating that he remains a prolific attacking threat.

Manchester United are also interested in the former Brentford striker, while Crystal Palace are exploring a potential reunion between Toney and Thomas Frank.

A recent CaughtOffside report revealed that a loan agreement with an option to buy is being explored, potentially offering interested clubs a more financially manageable route to signing him.

A move for Toney would represent a different approach from Arsenal’s recent recruitment strategy, but it could make sense under the right circumstances.

The England international offers proven Premier League experience, excellent hold-up play, aerial strength and reliable finishing. His ability to bring teammates into play would also suit Arsenal’s attacking system.

With Viktor Gyökeres and Kai Havertz among Arteta’s central attacking options, however, there is little justification for committing an enormous transfer fee or offering Toney a lucrative long-term contract.

A short-term loan would be considerably more attractive. It would give Arsenal additional firepower without compromising their ability to pursue younger attacking targets next summer.

Toney’s substantial wages in Saudi Arabia could complicate negotiations, but if a reasonable financial agreement can be reached, Arsenal should seriously consider the opportunity.

Having another proven goalscorer available during the decisive months of the campaign could make a significant difference to their trophy ambitions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Como presently sit in third place in the Champions League table with four victories from their first five games in 2026-27, and only one team has had a better start to their first season in the competition after the Champions League rebrand in 1992.

Como defeated AEK 1-0 at home on Tuesday evening to pick up their fourth win in their first five Champions League matches; Luis Milla providing the only goal of the game.

Industry observers note that cesc Fabregas’s side have also beaten RB Leipzig 4-1 this season, Manchester United 4-1 and Lens 9-1 away from home, the biggest winning margin by an away side in Champions League history. Feyenoord are the only team to have got the better of Como in Europe so far.

Sitting comfortably in third place with 12 points after five matches, and now targeting a top eight and a guaranteed spot in the round of 16, Como have started their first ever season in the Champions League in impressive fashion.

In fact, since 1992, only one team has enjoyed a better start to their first season in the Champions League: That was Leicester City back in 2016-17, off the back of their against-all-odds Premier League victory the season prior.

Under the guidance of Claudio Ranieri, the Foxes won four and drew one of their first five matches in the Champions League, which was enough to secure qualification to the knock-out rounds with one group stage match to spare.

Tottenham are already in talks over their first January transfer window deal, according to reports in Turkey.

Roberto De Zerbi's methods and philosophy are starting to permeate through the playing squad, and while the Italian's teams are normally known for their free-flowing, high-press, attacking football, his Tottenham team is set up with defensive solidity first and foremost.

Tottenham have the second-best Expected Goals Conceded statistics in the top flight so far, only just behind league leaders Arsenal, showing their defensive nous.

That is because Richarlison, the club's top scorer in all competitions in 2025/26, was left out of the 25-man Premier League squad entirely, following a falling out with De Zerbi over his future. De Zerbi initially described Richarlison as having an "unbelievable" attitude, but admitted that he had been left confused by the striker changing his mind over whether or not he wanted to stay at the club.

The Brazilian had been in talks over a move to Everton and Turkish side Trabzonspor in the late stages of the summer transfer window, but a move away did not come to fruition and the 29-year-old is now in the wilderness at Hotspur Way, training and playing with the U21s.

But talks are already underway between Tottenham and Trabzonspor, over a potential move in the January transfer window.

Turkish journalist Yagiz Sabuncuoglu has reported that talks have already taken place between the two clubs and that Spurs are demanding a €10million (£8million).

De Zerbi will be keen to see the Brazilian leave the club in the winter, rather than having someone at the club who is not part of his aims for the second half of the season.
