📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This live blog is now closed. Read on for a roundup of the top stories from and about Germany on the weekend of November 14-15, 2026:.

Thank you for reading this weekend's Germany news blog.

We'll bring you more from the heart of Europe on Monday. We wish you a very Schönen Abend!

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen has urged Europeans to defend compassion and humanity during Germany's national day of mourning for victims of war and oppression.

Speaking at a ceremony in the Bundestag in Berlin, Van der Bellen warned against becoming desensitized to suffering despite the constant images of war and violence.

"Compassion is not a weakness; it is a human strength; it is the foundation of humanity," he remarked.

He also addressed the responsibility of later generations for the crimes of the past.

Although people today bore no personal guilt for their ancestors' actions, he said, they were responsible for what they learned from history and how they treated others.

"Let us ensure that our home, Europe, remains a place where people can live in peace, freedom and dignity," he noted.

Bundestag President Julia Klöckner also called for the defense of democracy, pointing to Ukrainians risking their lives to protect freedom.

Germany's Volkstrauertag commemorates soldiers and civilians killed in war, as well as victims of Nazi persecution and other forms of oppression.

German police have arrested three suspects after thieves rammed a car into a jewelry store in the Bavarian city of Bayreuth and stole valuables worth around €10,000 ($11,600).

Bavarian Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann stated the stolen items included jewelry and silver coins.

The burglars drove a car into the store early in the morning before fleeing in a second vehicle, police mentioned.

Officers spotted the getaway car on the A9 highway and gave chase. The suspects left the highway near Weidensees, abandoned their vehicle beside a wooded area and fled on foot.

Police debuted a search involving patrol cars, dogs, drones and a helicopter.

All three suspects were subsequently arrested, with some of the stolen goods recovered.

Prosecutors are expected to decide whether to seek pretrial detention for the suspects.

It has been revealed that detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown played his first NFL American football game in Germany in Munich.

According to recent reports, st. Brown made his professional debut in Germany as the Detroit Lions faced the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena. The 27-year-old grew up in Southern California, and his mother, Miriam, is from Leverkusen. Both his parents were due to watch from the stands.

The NFL player spent childhood summers with his grandparents in the Rhineland.

"This is awesome. A dream come true," St. Brown said before the game. Asked by German broadcaster RTL what he had been looking forward to most, he reeled off a list that included schnitzel, potato dumplings, sauerkraut, currywurst and fries with mayonnaise.

Industry observers note that "I'm really excited. I can't wait," he remarked. "Being in Germany with my teammates and my family — I want to enjoy it and take it all in.".

Two people were slightly injured after an unidentified man threw a firework into the entrance of a gay bar in Frankfurt, police said.

The attack took place at the Zum Schwejk bar, a venue popular with the city's gay community, on Saturday evening.

Police mentioned the bar was clearly identifiable as an LGBTQ+ venue because of a rainbow flag displayed outside.

The motive remains unclear, and police have not mentioned whether they suspect a homophobic attack.

Officers are investigating suspected aggravated assault and have appealed for witnesses.

In a recent development, the bar stated it was "shocked and stunned" by the incident and apologized to guests who witnessed it. It said it wanted to be a place where everyone felt welcome, respected and safe, and pledged to do everything it could to prevent a repeat.

Andreas Ewald, LGBTQ+ policy spokesperson for the Greens in the Hesse state parliament, condemned the attack and called for those responsible to face the full force of the law.

He also urged the state government to establish a roundtable on LGBTQ+ safety involving community representatives, police and victim support organizations.

The bar's name refers to a Czech soldier in the satirical anti-war novel "The Good Soldier Svejk.".

Police in Berlin have filed 28 criminal charges against demonstrators who marched throught the capital on Saturday as part of the Gen Z regelt (Gen Z Takes Charge) movement.

Some 1,200 demonstrators took part in the march, although only 100 had registered for the event under German laws regulating public protests.

The protesters complained about dilapidated schools, the threat of compulsory military service, cuts to university and social funding and other complications.

Industry observers note that police said there had been some clashes with participants. A police spokeswoman said the criminal charges were filed for riot, assault, resisting officers and violations of explosives regulations.

Three police officers of the 700 deployed to ensure securty were injured during the demonstration.

November 20 is likely to see more large protests in both Germany and Europe, with some 15,000 demonstrators registered for a march in Berlin.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has expressed solidarity with the Jewish community in Germany amid what he described as ever "louder and more aggressive" antisemitic voices.

Speaking at the presentation of the Prize for Understanding and Tolerance awarded by the Jewish Museum in Berlin, Steinmeier noted: "For all those to whom our country, its constitution and the values it enshrines mean something, there can be only one answer to such antisemitism: to stand side by side with Jewish people in our country.".

Steinmeier stated he deplored the frequent vandalism of memorials to Nazi crimes.

"I am profoundly ashamed of that all," he remarked, saying that anyone who mocked the work of museums and memorial sites or collectively blamed, threatened and attacked Jews "attacks the heart of our republic.".

The president also congratulated the prize winners — German journalist and author Düzen Tekkal and British philanthropist Michael Moritz — on their awards.

In a citation, the museum described Tekkal as a champion of human rights who consistently opposed antisemitism and racism while promoting interfaith dialogue, equality in education and opportunities, peace and democracy.

The museum commended Moritz for supporting artistic projects that show Jewish perspectives and strengthen social dialogue.

The Jewish Museum, which is marking its 25th anniversary this year, has been presenting the prize since 2002.

Some 600 sheep have made their way through the southern city of Nuremberg on their way to western winter pasturage, watched by crowds of spectators.

The sheep follow an around 10-km-long (6-mile-long) route that crosses a number of streets and the market square.

The annual event is meant, among other things, to draw attention to the tradition of transhumant, or itinerant, sheep-keeping in the region and the benefits the animals have for landscape conservation.

"With their grazing in summer, sheep create great biodiversity in many important biotopes in the urban region," the city of Nuremberg remarked ahead of the migration.

Thieves have stolen several valuable items from a jewelry shop in the southern city of Bayreuth after ramming it with a car, police stated on Sunday.

They stated a black Mercedes carrying three people crashed into the shop in the early hours of Sunday morning.

The burglars then fled the scene in a second Mercedes, this time a gray one, after taking a number of articles.

The getaway car was then spotted by a police patrol on a motorway heading south, with officers setting off in pursuit.

The suspects were then said to have driven off the motorway to a patch of woodland where they abandoned their vehicle and went on by foot.

Police searched for the fugitives with patrol cars, police dogs, drones and a helicopter, a statement remarked.

Two men were reportedly arrested with a third still on the run. Investigators are looking into whether the detainees were connected with the theft.

Events are taking place around Germany for the Volkstrauertag (people's day of mourning), a day on which armed forces personnel and civilians who died in armed conflicts and victims of violent state oppression are commemorated.

Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen is to speak in the parliament at the main commemoration ceremony of the German War Graves Commission at midday.

His presence reflects the large number of Austrians who were killed in action in the Second World War while fighting for the German Wehrmacht following the annexation of their country by Nazi Germany in 1938.

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the patron of the commission, will also hold a speech and lay a wreath.

Last year, Steinmeier decreed that the Volkstrauertag should also commemorate people who were persecuted and killed by the Nazis because of their sexual identity, as well as police officers who have lost their lives in the course of duty.

There will also be a remembrance ceremony at the Jewish Cemetery in Berlin for those of the Jewish faith killed in World War I.

In remarks to the DPA news agency ahead of the remembrance day, the speaker of the lower house of German parliament, or Bundestag, Julia Klöckner, called on society to actively defend democracy.

Klöckner said that the Volkstrauertag was a reminder of how destructive tyranny and contempt for human dignity can be.

Recent findings suggest that "Democracy is the antidote here," she said. "But it is not an heirloom. It wastes away when we do not constantly renew its promise of basic rights and freedom.".

Guten Morgen from the DW newsroom on the banks of the Rhine in Bonn!

You join us as Germany holds a day of remembrance for the victims of war and oppression and also commemorates members of the police force killed while carrying out their duties.

It's 1 a.m. here and time for us to pause our coverage of news from Germany.

We'll be back Sunday morning with more of what's making headlines in Berlin, Bavaria and the rest of the country.

Germany wants to turn its spies into "real secret agents." A sweeping reform could allow them to sabotage threats abroad and use AI to analyze intelligence data.

But why does Germany need these powers now? And how far can its secret services go in a country with a history of strict limits on intelligence operations?

Hundreds of mourners gathered at Munich's Frauenkirche on Saturday to pay their final respects to Hubert Aiwanger, Bavaria's former deputy premier and economy minister, who died unexpectedly at the age of 55.

The ceremony combined a Catholic funeral Mass with a state memorial service, attended by leading political figures, church representatives and members of Bavaria's former royal family.

Bavarian Premier Markus Söder recalled his disbelief when he first heard of Aiwanger's death in a Berlin hotel on November 4. He described his former deputy as someone who had always been full of energy.

Bavarian parliament president Ilse Aigner praised Aiwanger as one of the greatest political talents of his generation, highlighting his role in transforming his party "Freie Wähler" (Free Voters) from a local political movement into a governing party.

Aiwanger's partner, Tanja Schweiger, and their two sons were among those attending the service, which took place eleven days after his death.

German airline group Lufthansa says it was only slightly affected by Friday's temporary suspension of flights to the United States.

Most flights operated as scheduled, although some were canceled or delayed. Lufthansa expects its US flight schedule to return to normal on Saturday but warned that isolated delays could still occur.

Affected passengers are being notified by email, with alternative travel options provided automatically in the event of cancellations.

The disruption was caused by problems with the US air traffic control system. Domestic flights in the US were grounded for around four hours, marking the longest nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks in 2001.

The real reason why United States women's national soccer team star Trinity Rodman and tennis ace Ben Shelton split up has emerged following their high-profile break-up.

Rodman, daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman, and Shelton went public with their relationship in March 2025 after rumours sparked on social media.

They became a sporting power couple and frequently supported one another at various events, including Shelton's impressive run at this year's US Open.

He reached the first Grand Slam final of his budding career, beating the likes of Carlos Alcaraz and fellow countryman Frances Tiafoe. However, he fell short in his bid to become US Open champion following his defeat to Alexander Zverev in four sets.

The 24-year-old forward was captured crying inside Arthur Ashe Stadium following the world No.4's crushing defeat to Zverev, who was accused of flirting with her in his post-match victory speech.

After nearly two years together, Rodman and Shelton have split up. That's according to The Daily Mail, who have revealed they have recently decided to call time on their blossoming relationship.

Per the report, their conflicting work schedules and constant travel made it 'too challenging for the couple to continue maintaining their relationship', given Shelton is traveling around the world while playing on the ATP Tour, with his latest venture taking him to Turin, Italy, for the ATP Finals, where he lost to Alcaraz in the semi-finals.

Rodman was also in action the same evening as the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final to the KC Current.

They attempted to make it work, with multiple sacrifices and last-minute trips to attend each other's matches, but it appears the strain has taken its toll, resulting in their split.

Despite ending their romance, Rodman and Shelton are believed to remain close.

Shelton also travelled long distances to support Rodman during their relationship, including the 7,300-mile trip from Shanghai to Chester, Pennsylvania, for USWNT's game against Spain last month.

A month prior to watching Rodman compete for her national team, Shelton opened up on the challenges of their relationship, revealing that it was tough for them to continuously make time for one another due to their busy workload.

Speaking to US Weekly, he admitted: "It is really difficult.

"I think what a lot of people don't see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we're so exhausted that it's tough to do anything. It is tough to make time.".

The 24-year-old added: "Sometimes I leave these tournaments and I'm a bit of a zombie. I'm not the most fun person to be around. But we make a lot of sacrifices for our sport. I'd say both of us are chasing things for our sport. We're not where we want to be yet, we're not in our primes. So this is kind of crunch time.

"This is going to be the hardest, most grueling time in our relationship, from my perspective. None of it is easy. But being able to have someone to lean on who's such an elite athlete and doing things at a really high level as well, it helps in so many ways.".

Bartesaghi started for Milan in their first game back after the recent international break over the weekend, which ended in a 5-1 victory at home against Frosinone in Serie A.

Milan now have a list of nine players who will not be able to feature in Athens on Thursday night: Bartesaghi and Camarda add to an injury list that already included Luka Modric, Strahinja Pavlovic, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers, Samuel Chukwueze, Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Pietro Terracciano.

Recent findings suggest that it will be a tough test for the Rossoneri on Thursday night, up against an Olympiacos side that sit among the top eight after winning three of their first four matches in the Europa League. Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Industry observers note that but United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

In a recent development, however, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday.

In a recent development, ‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving swiftly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’.

In a recent development, united sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ stated Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’.

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a latest contact stalled.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We have time to speak about that,’ stated Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’.

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’.

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
  • Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the news spread from one mathematician to the next, panic set in. On 6 October, OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, released more than 700 preprints written by AI, claiming to have solved more than 300 major open problems in mathematics. Some researchers stayed up all night combing through the papers that the firm had posted, anxious to know whether their entire research programmes had been rendered obsolete overnight.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Mathematicians astounded by AI and human-written proofs of iconic Riemann hypothesis.

Depending on who you ask, this was either the most progress or the most catastrophic development ever to happen in one day in the history of the field — or both. Either way, mathematicians realized that their profession would never be the same. “It’s probably the end of mathematics as we know it,” theoretical physicist Miranda Cheng said at an emergency meeting on mathematics and AI at the Royal Society in London in late October. Many of the papers cracked problems by combining ideas from disparate parts of the discipline, leveraging a universality of knowledge that no human could ever match — and leaving even some of the world’s smartest people feeling completely outdone.

Since then, one of the field’s greatest outstanding challenges, the Riemann hypothesis, also appears to have been solved with AI assistance. And mathematicians across the world have joined frantic collective efforts to confront challenges raised by AI’s advances, from how to evaluate and publish research papers to how to raise future generations of mathematicians. Some see the risk as existential. If mathematical problem-solving becomes mainly a machine endeavour — seen as a utility like water or electricity — then their profession could lose its status in society and human expertise might start to dwindle.

“It’s a challenge like we’ve never faced in mathematics — or in academia as a whole,” says Simon Machado, a mathematician at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) in Zurich.

The bombshell paper drop in October came on the heels of earlier shocks to the field. OpenAI, which is based in San Francisco, California, released a batch of ten crucial results in August and, in early September, followed up with a historic solution to the Navier–Stokes problem about how fluids flow. The firm had been making noises to indicate that much more was to come. Still, many researchers were surprised by the enormity of the 6 October release. “To just see it as a giant list, without the care and thought and the love that goes into doing this work on a normal basis, it was really jarring,” indicates Catherine Cossaboom, a master’s student in mathematics at the University of Oxford, UK.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms.

Sources indicate that perhaps no source has documented the moment better than Proofs and Prompts, an online forum that publishes essays on the impact of AI on mathematics. An 8 October post titled “100+ reactions to 100+ solutions” collected immediate reactions from dozens of students and career researchers to OpenAI’s 6 October drop. Some wrote poems, others quoted the writers Leo Tolstoy and Stanisław Lem, still others posted fragments from the Gospels (in the original Greek). One contribution reinterpreted the lyrics of ‘Jolene’ by the late country singer Dolly Parton:.

And I can easily understand / How you could easily take my math / But you don’t know what it means to me, AI.

It has been revealed that the tone ranged from the enthusiastic to the angry and the despondent. “Some of them made me really feel heartbroken,” states Albane Théry, an applied mathematician at the University of Warwick in Coventry, UK, who is one of the volunteer moderators of the forum.

According to recent reports, few subfields of mathematics were spared and some were thoroughly ravaged. “Not a single one of the major open problems I have publicly mentioned throughout my career was left untouched,” Fields Medal winner Hugo Duminil-Copin wrote to Proofs and Prompts. “I expected that one day we would be surpassed, and that it would happen systematically. But yesterday’s announcement hit with a force I had not anticipated.”.

Hugo Duminil-Copin fears that AI will eclipse human understanding of mathematics.Credit: Chris Peus.

Recent findings suggest that duminil-Copin, who is at the University of Geneva in Switzerland, specializes in the theory of transitions in complex systems — such as those that determine how information or infection filters through social networks or how metals can acquire magnetization. (OpenAI’s rival Anthropic, also in San Francisco, had already claimed to have solved a major result in this field in late August.).

It has been revealed that another field that bore a massive impact was the theory of groups — some of the most ubiquitous structures across mathematics, physics and other disciplines. For example, the possible ways of shuffling a deck of cards — and what happens when you revert a shuffle or combine several together — constitute a group, as do the infinite possible ways of rotating a solid object in 3D.

It has been revealed that openAI’s August batch already contained the solution to a key problem on groups. Soon after its release, during a YouTube interview, Francesco Fournier-Facio, a group theorist at Heriot-Watt University in Edinburgh, UK, mentioned two other problems that mathematicians could now attack with the help of AI. Within days, he was emailed by a PhD student in computational biology who had used OpenAI’s large language model (LLM) GPT 5.6 Sol to solve one of those problems.

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

According to recent reports, can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world.

Industry observers note that fournier-Facio claims that OpenAI’s October dump was even more impactful for him personally. It included the solution to a problem on which he had been actively working, called the Boone–Higman conjecture. Overall, OpenAI released solutions to perhaps eight of the top ten problems that Fournier-Facio had dreamed of solving during his career, he told Nature.

Industry observers note that but the most stunning AI result relates to what many researchers see as the most crucial open problem in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis, a question that was posed in the mid-nineteenth century by the German mathematician Bernhard Riemann, centres on whether prime numbers are scattered across the set of all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as unpredictable as it could be.

AI assistance seems to have cracked it. First, OpenAI proved a partial result, called the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, in its October dump. Then, on 20 November, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge announced that he had found a proof of the full Riemann hypothesis, working with Claude, the firm’s AI assistant. However, that was quickly followed by a non-AI assisted proof by Rome-based mathematician Alessandro Masullo, which he had been working on for years. “If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” notes number theorist James Maynard, a Fields Medal winner at the University of Oxford.

Maynard and many other researchers are excited by AI technology. It is “quite likely to unleash a golden age of mathematical discovery”, he said at the meeting. Another mathematician, Antoine Tilloy at the Mines Paris engineering school, part of PSL University, uses the metaphor that doing mathematics with AI is like riding a dragon: the researcher is still in charge, but the dragon gives them supernatural powers.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption.

In a recent development, but the speed at which AI proofs are emerging has already produced an immediate negative reaction. For one, mathematicians, who have long prided themselves on their field’s culture of openness, are now wary of discussing their work in public. “People are even scared to put out an abstract for a talk they are about to give on ongoing work,” states Jakub Dobrowolski, a PhD candidate at Queen Mary University of London. “Nobody wants to share upcoming ideas because of the speed at which somebody else can take them and write a paper,” says Peter Sarnak, a number theorist at Princeton University in New Jersey.

In a recent development, and although established researchers say that they are both thrilled and anxious about reinventing their discipline with AI, younger generations are much more fearful. As Maynard and other established mathematicians acknowledge, the technology already poses severe problems in relation to how to assess merit when peer-reviewing mathematics work that might have been done mostly with AI, and how to train and educate the next generation of mathematicians.

In a recent development, “How do we train people if a good PhD thesis can be prompted out of an LLM? The response from people who are in permanent positions tends to be ‘We’re going to see and discuss’,” claims Théry. “But the timescale for that could be too long for postdoc or PhD candidates who will be out of a job in nine months.”.

In a recent development, many early-career researchers told Nature that this uncertainty is their main source of anxiety right now. “While it is clear that faculty are working hard to find long-term solutions to the problems we are all facing, there doesn’t seem to be as much guidance on what to do in the meantime,” notes Jad Hamdan, a postdoc mathematician at the University of Oxford. AI poses “more danger the younger you are, and the less experienced you are”, adds Dobrowolski. The toughest problem could be working out how to write a proposal for a research programme that might span two or three years, or more, Dobrowolski says. “Is it realistic? Now I feel like whatever I propose might just expire within a year.”.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow.

A UK survey of graduate students and academic mathematicians last month by the Martingale Foundation in London found that PhD students in particular are much less optimistic about AI’s impact than are established researchers. Asked if AI would “weaken their development as mathematicians”, 89% of students agreed, compared with only 68% of academics.

Breaking: Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1180 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.
  • Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk.
  • Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws.

Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk. The Polish prime minister pledged to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy before the 2023 parliamentary election, but his coalition has been unable to agree on a common position.

Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.

In Poland, abortion is only allowed when the pregnancy is the result of a crime — rape or incest — or when it endangers the health or life of the woman.

Justyna Wydrzynska, an activist from a nonprofit organization called Abortion Dream Team, showed DW the "Abortomat" in a small room behind a tasseled portiere at Abotak, Poland's first abortion center.

Industry observers note that inside, the pink lighting is subdued. Glitter tassels, baubles and spotlights make it feel a bit like a disco, she remarked.

Industry observers note that the "Abortomat," which opened in late September, has 22 pink lockers. To open one, a woman receives a PIN code from the organization Women Help Women after completing a medical questionnaire, which is then checked by a doctor.

Recent findings suggest that parcel lockers have sprung up like mushrooms after rain in Poland in recent years. Even the smallest villages have them.

It has been revealed that "When you walk around Poland, vending machines are everywhere. This is our culture. People in the US have Amazon, we have vending machines for everything," noted Wydrzynska.

Women in Poland who have an abortion are not criminalized. But anyone who helps them terminate a pregnancy risks up to three years in prison.

In 2023, Wydrzynska was the first activist to be convicted in Poland of helping a woman to have an abortion by sending her pills. The conviction was later overturned, and the court ordered a retrial.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Inside each compartment at the "Abortomat" is a package that normally contains two drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol, usually taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy.

Because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, the drug must be ordered from abroad where it is legal. Information on how to do this is not easy to come by, which is where Abortion Dream Team and Abotak come in. They help women find information about accessing medication, which is sent from abroad by Women Help Women, or help them to travel abroad for a termination.

Wydrzynska noted she believes the "Abortomat" does not break the law because it is a machine, not a person, that is delivering the pills, although she admits she is not sure.

Dr. Sabrina Mana-Walasek, a reproductive rights lawyer representing Wydrzynska, said the legal environment for abortion pills is "complicated.".

She said that although mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it is registered in the European Union and, as EU citizens, Polish women can order it and take it.

"If a woman orders pills for herself and pays for them herself, it's not a crime," she mentioned.

The ultra-Catholic legal group Ordo Iuris disagrees and has notified the prosecutor's office that the activists are committing a crime.

"In the case of an 'Abortomat,' the actions enabling a woman to have an abortion are theoretically performed by the woman herself using the device, but the reality is that this machine is operated by people — they send the code required to open the compartment containing abortion pills, they order and procure the pills, and they restock the compartments," said Katarzyna Gesiak, director of the Ordo Iuris Center for Medical Law and Bioethics.

Wydrzynska said anti-abortion activists regularly demonstrate outside Abotak, using horns and loudspeakers to generate loud noise to annoy the center's residential neighbors and pressure the landlord to revoke their rental agreement.

At one demonstration, a woman holding an image of the Virgin Mary told DW she believes abortion "is the work of Satan.".

"Abortion is evil, it's demonic, it's against the fifth Commandment, 'Thou shalt not kill,'" she stated.

Earlier this year, Diana, a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman living in Warsaw, used abortion pills during her sixth week of pregnancy before the "Abortomat" started up. She got the pills using information provided by Abortion Dream Team.

Diana told DW that she has never wanted to have children.

It has been revealed that "I was expecting something like a headache, stomachache, maybe vomiting, but I had nothing like that. It was just like a normal period. I didn't feel any pain. It was really easy for me," she noted.

According to recent reports, "I felt relief because I knew that it was the right choice for me. I knew that I can live my life," she added.

According to recent reports, another Abortion Dream Team activist, Natalia Broniarczyk, remarked they help about 130 women daily in Poland. About 125 of these women use pills that cost about €75 ($83), while the remainder travel to a clinic abroad.

In contrast, just 851 abortions were performed in Polish hospitals last year.

Broniarczyk is concerned about the rising support for right-wing parties ahead of next year's parliamentary election, but she's also furious at the inactivity of liberals in Tusk's coalition.

"I'm mad at the liberals because for three years, they did nothing to protect us. They lost three years and now, when we're close to an election, they are fighting for our voices and respect. People are more progressive than politicians," she stated.

After taking office in 2023, Tusk's coalition, which includes left-wing and conservative partners, were unable to agree a common position and their separate bills failed to obtain parliamentary approval in 2024.

Afterwards, Tusk stated abortion on request would not be possible during the current parliamentary term.

In October, however, two bills were resubmitted to the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, and were narrowly approved.

One reinstates severe irreversible fetal defects as a justification for a legal termination. This justification had been ruled illegal by the Constitutional Court in 2020 when the previous right-wing Law and Justice (PiS)-led government was in power.

The 2020 ruling led to tens of thousands of people, mostly women, taking part in street protests in towns and cities across the country, some of the largest since communism fell in 1989.

Lawmakers also approved a bill partially decriminalizing anyone who helps a woman terminate her pregnancy.

According to the results of a recent poll conducted by SW Research for Onet.pl, almost 61% of respondents said they want the country's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, to sign into law the bill on the fetal defect justification.

Nawrocki opposes abortion, and both Wydrzynska and Broniarczyk think he will use his power of veto to block the bills, preventing them from becoming law.

When Liverpool fans chanted about Mauricio Pochettino's job security just 15 minutes into his first game in charge of Manchester United, who instantly found themselves 2-0 down at Anfield, it acted as a timely reminder of just how entertaining football supporters can be.

In a recent development, even when watching their side lose every week, they get creative. Perhaps if they don't laugh, they will cry at the state of their team. Either way, it has made for some fairly hilarious moments over the years.

Whether it's because a player has shared a name with a shop or the thought of their feet sticking out the bed, there have been plenty of funny chants across the world of football and GiveMeSport has ranked them.

Sometimes, the best thing to do when watching your team lose is to join the mockery, and that's exactly what Norwich City fans have done in the past.

Fed up of waiting for a goal, the Canaries simply chanted about having possession, starting their chant with "we've won the ball", before singing "we've lost the ball" as soon as possession was conceded.

"We've won the ball, we've won the ball, we've won the ball,.

"We've lost the ball, we've lost the ball, we've lost the ball".

Players can't get away with anything, can they? It's like fans are the flies on the wall in the dressing room at times and when Jason Puncheon left the pitch midway through the second-half of Southampton's game against Everton in 2013, they knew exactly what he was going to do.

When Puncheon re-emerged, fans welcomed him back onto the pitch by chanting:.

"Jason Puncheon, he went for a s***.".

Weeks later, the former Southampton man celebrates by pretending to sit on the toilet in his goal celebration. When a man's got to go, a man's got to go...

Jonjo Shelvey's so-called resemblance to infamous Harry Potter villain Voldemort is unfortunate, to say the least, and it didn't take long for West Ham fans to take notice.

They mocked the then-Liverpool midfielder during his warm-up by chanting all about Voldemort's biggest rival.

"He's coming for you, he's coming for you, Harry Potter, he's coming for you.".

It has been revealed that the song has followed Shelvey round for the rest of his career ever since. Awkward.

It could be the worst moment of a player's career, but that doesn't matter for football fans. Chelsea picked the perfect moment to rub salt in Steven Gerrard's wounds in 2014, when his slip allowed Demba Ba to all but end Liverpool's Premier League title hopes at Anfield of all places.

Fans instantly got creative, turning Liverpool's Gerrard song into a version of their own, mocking the Anfield captain for how he cost his side what would have been their first Premier League title at the time.

"Steve Gerrard, Gerrard, he slipped on his f****** a***,.

"He passed the ball to Demba Ba, Steve Gerrard, Gerrard.".

In a recent development, give football fans a trendy song and they'll have a player's name involved within the hour. At Celtic, it was the Pussycat Dolls' 'Don't Cha' song which took their interest, as they turned it into a song for right-back Cha Du-Ri.

The Bhoys serenaded their defender with the new version of the song, and it remains one of the most catchy chants that Scottish football fans have ever produced.

Recent findings suggest that "Don't Cha wish your full back was Cha Du-Ri? Don't Cha? Don't Cha?".

Poor Filip Sebo didn't go a second without a moment of humiliation in Scotland. The former Rangers forward swiftly became known for his horror misses and ended his Ibrox career with just two goals to his name.

This initially handed Celtic fans plenty of ammunition. The Bhoys would chant his name whenever he missed a sitter in front of his own fans, much to the frustration of those at Ibrox.

The Gers soon flipped the script, however, and joined in the mocking of their transfer flop.

"Sebo's on, we're taking the p***,.

"Sebo's on, we're taking the p***".

Anyone else struggle to even think about the original 'Freed From Desire' song these days? Whenever it is played, it instantly becomes the Will Grigg song all over again.

Sources indicate that wigan Athletic fans went viral after turning the song into a tune about their striker following his 28-goal season in 2016 and it has followed his career ever since. It is one of the most viral and funniest chants that football fans have ever come up with.

"Will Griggs on fire, your defence is terrified,.

Will Griggs on fire, your defence is terrified,.

Will Griggs on fire, your defence is terrified,.

Will Griggs on fire Na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na, na...".

It feels fitting that Peter Crouch has one of the funniest chants in football. The towering striker was one of the biggest characters back in his playing days, quite literally and figuratively speaking.

Sources indicate that liverpool fans didn't always see the best of their striker, but that didn't stop them from singing his name. Dedicating a song to his absurd height, Anfield claimed that Crouch was so tall that his feet stuck out the bed.

"He's major, he's red, his feet stick out the bed, Peter Crouch, Peter Crouch.".

When Sunderland appointed Dick Advocacaat in 2015, Sunderland fans had an opportunity that they were never going to let pass them by. And so, when they travelled to face West Ham, they did so with a large inflatable object in reference to their manager's first name.

The fun didn't last long, however, as stewards soon confiscated that inflatable object, leading to a hilarious chant from the travelling Black Cats about getting it back.

"We want our d*** back, we want our d*** back, we want our d*** back.".

There's not much worse than travelling to watch your team face Hull City and then hearing the 'mauled by the Tigers' song alongside the clawing hand gesture.

It has become a tool of mockery for the home fans whenever they find themselves on the winning side and the likes of Brighton and Man United have all faced a mauling.

It is arguably one of the best chants in the Premier League right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Luciano Spalletti has confirmed that Jeff Ekhator is set to play for Juventus in their Europa League match against Omonoia on Thursday evening, says that Kenan Yildiz is progressing well in his recovery from injury, but grew frustrated when asked about his striker situation during his pre-match press conference on Wednesday.

Juventus are due to take on Omonoia at the Allianz Stadium at 20.00 GMT on Thursday evening in their fifth match of the Europa League season.

According to recent reports, the Bianconeri have started encouragingly in the Europa League with three victories and one draw across their first four matches, which has them in fifth place ahead of this week’s round of fixtures. Omonoia have won two and lost two of their first four games, leaving them in 18th place on six points.

It has been revealed that spalletti’s press conference began with a quick injury patch. The Bianconeri are without long-term absentees Yildiz, Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli, and will also remain without Nico Gonzalez or Pierre Kalulu on Thursday night.

“We have got some players back, except for Nico and Kalulu, the others are available. We have to prepare as best we can because training sessions are starting to get busier. That is a positive, though.”.

Spalletti then grew frustrated when asked for clarification on his recent comments about wanting a new striker in January.

Speaking after Juventus’s 4-0 win over Venezia in Serie A over the weekend, Spalletti had discussed the characteristics of his current striking options. Neither Randal Kolo Muani nor Nick Woltemade are considered ‘traditional’ no.9s and Ekhator has been impacted by injuries since joining.

There have been suggestions that Juventus could move for a physically imposing centre-forward in January, but Spalletti was not pleased at his comments being labeled a ‘desperate cry’ for intervention in the transfer window.

“Calling it a ‘desperate cry’ were your words, not mine,” Spalletti argued. “How many times have you asked me about Vlahovic? Even after he left. I spoke about the need for certain characteristics, not a certain player.

In a recent development, “I want to try Kolo in a different position. Woltemade has done very well since coming in, but can’t play all the time. I thought I would put Kolo Muani back there [at centre-forward] for the Venezia game. That was not a desperate cry. I never noted that I don’t like Woltemade. We also have Ekhator now and we have to see how he’s doing. He’s a promising young player, we’ll let him play a few times and see if we already have those qualities in-house. When Nico returns, he also has the qualities of a no.9.”.

Returning to the topic of tomorrow’s game, Spalletti gave his assessment of the visiting Omonoia.

“Omonia is a team that has picked up six points and beat Celta Vigo. They’re third in their league and have a Norwegian coach who knows modern football very well. They’re a team that plays in a 4-2-3-1 but they are willing to sacrifice and go into a five when they defend. They’ve struggled in some matches, but they always create difficulty for their opponents. We will need to play a very serious game to win.

Recent findings suggest that “We have a lot of top quality players and they’re all good. We also need to develop some young players. We’ll play Ekhator tomorrow because we want an extra solution moving forwards. We will make rotations that we trust in. We’re aware of what is at stake.”.

Industry observers note that commenting further on Ekhator’s qualities, Spalletti added: “I think he’s a physical striker who attacks the space well. He’s a player who makes bad balls playable. Baldini speaks very highly of him and Baldini is one of my close friends within football. I’m getting to know him a bit better now and I agree with Baldini.

“I expect him to be calm, but he’s a player with good prospects and all great players started out as a talent with good prospects before reaching that level.”.

Spalletti also offered an encouraging patch on Yildiz, who has not featured since the first game of the Serie A season.

“He’s doing great. This morning, he started a specialised training session and I can’t wait to have him back in games. We have to wait for the right timing. Being without a player of his level creates a void we somehow need to fill. Being able to replace him with Alajbegovic, Boga or Kolo is great, though, but Yildiz is a champion you can’t simply just replace.”.

In a recent development, laLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas claims Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

According to recent reports, earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez said Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

Industry observers note that tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

Industry observers note that the thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club said Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

Recent findings suggest that the same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas stated the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

Recent findings suggest that the dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that having done law at LSE, Vijievan transitioned into the world of sports journalism through a fast-track diploma course with the Press Association. After completing that, he did an internship at 90min, before joining the Snack Media team on a full-time basis.

Initially starting off as a writer for FootballFanCast, Vijievan became assistant editor of the site and weekend editor of This is Futbol. After a few years working across both sites, he took up the role of assistant editor to the exclusives project at GiveMeSport, speaking to a number of top journalists like Fabrizio Romano and Christian Falk on the latest transfer news across European football.

Now taking on the role of evergreen editor, Vijievan is responsible for longer-form content based on everything from the Premier League to international football. Outside of that, he's also passionate about cricket and the NBA.

Sources indicate that the hardest job in football is putting the ball in the back of the net, and it's no surprise that forwards who can do that on a regular basis often get paid the major bucks. Whether it's scoring a screamer from 30 yards or bundling home from a goalmouth scramble, the absolute best in the business don't just deliver in a one-off game, but can be relied upon week-in and week-out.

It has been revealed that erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe proved exactly that in the autumn of 2025, embarking on simultaneous scoring runs for club and country. Mbappe's came to a halt at 11 games against Juventus, while Haaland's reached 12 before Aston Villa finally kept the Manchester City striker quiet.

But as remarkable as Haaland's run was, it isn't the longest in football history. Using data available from European football's top five major leagues from the year 2000, find out below the 10 longest goal-scoring runs for both club and country the game has ever seen, including some familiar faces like Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Starting off this list, unsurprisingly, is Lionel Messi. The former Barcelona star actually had two separate streaks of ten games of goals, first in the autumn of 2010, when he scored for the Catalan giants as well as Argentina, before repeating the incredible feat with Barcelona alone across December 2012 and January 2013. The first of those runs brought 16 goals – 15 for Barcelona and one for his country.

The 2012/2013 season was particularly special as Messi claimed a record-breaking feat of scoring in 21 La Liga matches in a row, but his all-competition run stalled at ten, meaning his club and country record of scoring in consecutive games stayed at 'just' ten.

A man who has spent his entire career in Serie A after leaving South America, Duvan Zapata enjoyed his best spell in football while with Atalanta, with his performances during the 2018/2019 campaign especially noteworthy.

According to recent reports, his streak of 10 consecutive games of scoring a goal included a particularly dominant performance against Frosinone in January 2019, when he scored four times, becoming the first Atalanta player to do so in the league since Hasse Jeppson in 1952. Zapata's goals would fire the club to a superb third-placed finish in Serie A and the Coppa Italia final, bagging 23 times in the league alone.

Recent findings suggest that the first of two entries for Robert Lewandowski on this list, the Poland international can rightly be regarded as one of the greatest number nines of all-time. The fact he was still scoring regularly for Barcelona well into his late 30s, before swapping Catalonia for MLS side Chicago Fire in 2026 is only testament to his capabilities, but he was arguably at his absolute peak in a Bayern Munich shirt during the early 2020s.

Indeed, between May and August 2020, as football returned from the COVID-19 shutdown, Lewandowski scored in ten consecutive games in all competitions for Bayern. The run powered the club's charge to the treble, ending only in the Champions League final against PSG, where Kingsley Coman's header settled the contest, at a time where many believed he was due a Ballon d'Or.

Industry observers note that amid all the recent injuries and heartbreak, it's easy to forget that Neymar was one of the best players in the world during his time at Barcelona. The Brazilian would then, of course, make the big-money move to PSG to become part of their own version of the Galacticos. And while it didn't result in the Champions League title the Parisian club so desperately wanted, Neymar did produce some moments of magic that left the Parc des Princes in awe.

According to recent reports, his ten-game run straddled two seasons. It began in May 2022 as the 2021/22 campaign drew to a close, continued through Brazil's June friendlies, and carried on into a blistering start to 2022/23 – including the Trophée des Champions and PSG's opening Ligue 1 fixtures – before finally coming to an end at the start of September.

Once upon a time, Radamel Falcao was considered one of the greatest strikers in the world, enjoying hugely prolific spells at the likes of Porto, Atlético Madrid and AS Monaco. An ACL injury suffered while playing for the Ligue 1 side would then prove to be the start of an unfortunate decline that even counted spells in the Premier League at both Manchester United and Chelsea on loan.

Industry observers note that however, it was his time at Atlético that really saw his name be discussed among the greats, including an 11-game scoring streak in 2012 between August and October 2012 that featured a hat-trick against Chelsea in the UEFA Super Cup, which is one of his best-ever showings. Brilliant in the air and a deceptively quick player who could finish off both feet and with incredible ingenuity, Falcao even finished fifth in the 2012 Ballon d'Or race, coming only behind Messi, Ronaldo, Andrés Iniesta and Xavi.

Sources indicate that one record Cristiano Ronaldo has over Lionel Messi, is the longest goal-scoring streak for both club and country. While Messi's best effort was 10, CR7 managed to go one better and notched in 11 games straight, doing so between February and April 2014 while he was with Real Madrid and arguably at the peak of his athletic powers.

It has been revealed that what perhaps made Ronaldo's achievements all that greater, was the teams he scored against. As well as bagging three goals in two separate games against Los Blancos' arch-rivals Atlético Madrid, Ronaldo would also net in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund and the El Clásico against Barcelona.

Sources indicate that amid all the talk of Erling Haaland's incredible goal-scoring run to start off the 2025/2026 campaign, it's easy to forget Kylian Mbappe enjoyed a similarly prolific run in front of goal too. The France international netted in 11 consecutive games for club and country, scoring 15 total goals in the process.

The Real Madrid superstar bagged against Real Sociedad, Espanyol, Atlético Madrid, Villarreal, Getafe, Levante, Marseille and Kairat Almaty at club level, before also scoring at international level with Les Bleus against the likes of Ukraine, Iceland and Azerbaijan. His great run, however, came to an end when he failed to net in the Champions League clash against Juventus, when Jude Bellingham netted the only goal in a narrow 1-0 win.

Recent findings suggest that between March and May 2003, Ruud van Nistelrooy found the net in 12 straight games for club and country. The run mixed eight Premier League matches with both legs of Manchester United's Champions League quarter-final against Real Madrid and two internationals for the Netherlands.

Industry observers note that the league portion of that spell also made Premier League history. For quite a while, former Manchester United striker Ruud van Nistelrooy held the record for the most goals scored in consecutive games in just the Premier League alone. The Dutchman bagged in ten top-flight games straight from 22nd March 2003 to 23rd August 2003, which actually broke his own record of eight matches that he achieved just 19 months earlier.

It stood until Jamie Vardy scored in 11 successive Premier League games for Leicester City in 2015. Van Nistelrooy's goals during that run included a hat-trick against Fulham and a brace against arch-rivals Liverpool.

Haaland's start to the 2025/2026 campaign was nothing short of extraordinary, firing Man City back into the conversation of being Premier League and Champions League contenders again. The striker's feat began when he scored in the Premier League against Brighton, and he netted in each of City's next five top-flight games, including striking twice in a victory over Manchester United in the derby and netting in the 1-1 draw against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Sources indicate that haaland also bagged in all three of City's Champions League games during the run, scoring against Napoli, AS Monaco and Villarreal respectively. For Norway, he scored the winner against Finland in a friendly before hitting five against Moldova and a hat-trick against Israel in World Cup qualifying.

In all, he plundered 22 goals across the 12 games. The run finally ended in a 1-0 defeat at Aston Villa, where he thought he had equalised in the second half, only for the goal to be ruled out for offside.

The man who still at the moment holds the record for the most number of consecutive games of scoring, is none other than Robert Lewandowski. The striker was at the peak of his powers during his time at Bayern Munich, and having already netted in 10 games straight in 2020, he went even better just a year later. A streak of 14 games of scoring came for both Bayern and Poland, and it served to remind the world just why he was considered the ultimate number nine at the time.

Between February and May 2021, Lewandowski scored in ten Bundesliga games, both legs of Bayern's Champions League last-16 tie against Lazio and two World Cup qualifiers for Poland. The final goal of the run came on the last day of the season, as he struck a 41st Bundesliga goal of the campaign to break Gerd Muller's long-standing single-season record.

Data sourced from Transfermarkt (Stats correct as of 25/11/2026).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

The Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

The abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

Industry observers note that the man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid said in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

Industry observers note that the fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

According to recent reports, the case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

The ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

It has been revealed that the Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

For Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

Real Madrid is now acting as private prosecutor in other cases involving similar incidents against its players.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up?
  • Recent findings suggest that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen.
  • Recent findings suggest that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that is Germany's economy back on the up? The answer to that question depends on your perspective.

Recent findings suggest that at the 2026 Mechanical Engineering Summit in Berlin this week, the mood was sullen. "A year ago, I said here: We are angry. Today I must say: We are stunned," Bertram Kawlath, president of the Mechanical Engineering Industry Association (VDMA), said in his opening remarks on Tuesday.

Recent findings suggest that the mechanical and plant engineering sector was the backbone of German industry for decades. It once employed more than a million people; now 15,000 positions are being cut every month. Production has shrunk about 20% since 2018.

Kawlath criticized the federal government's infighting and lack of reform, as well as what the companies consider a continued high bureaucracy and tax burden.

"[We are] stunned by the whitewashing in so many government statements. Stunned by the increasingly visible decline of our country as a business location.".

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz promised quick reforms and a rapidly noticeable economic upswing when he took office in May 2025. A year and a half later, reality has caught up with him.

According to recent reports, merz's coalition of his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), its Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union, (CSU), along with the center-left Social Democrats(SPD), keeps running into trouble. In addition, there are crises and wars. The German economy is facing more headwinds than seldom before, Merz said in October at the German Employers' Day conference in Berlin.

Recent findings suggest that given the circumstances, small successes are even more meaningful. "A heartfelt thanks for the good news you bring," Merz said when he received the autumn report of the Council of Economic Experts in Berlin, which predicted economic growth of 1.3% for 2026 and 1% for 2027.

The economic experts have a German government mandate to independently analyze business activity and make recommendations for economic policy. Earlier this year, they were much more pessimistic.

According to recent reports, "The German economy has recovered quicker than expected from the energy price shock sparked by the war in Iran," mentioned Monika Schnitzer, chair of the expert advisory board, explaining the prognosis. "We see a significant economic recovery, driven by surprisingly strong exports and high government spending.".

The chancellor, who celebrated his 71st birthday on November 11, spoke of "encouraging signals" in his address. "The economy in Germany is slowly on the rise again. Considering the many crises in Germany, it was not totally expected that we would manage that.".

But these improved prospects do not change the long-term problems. An ageing society means the bills for pensions, health and caregiving are constantly rising.

At the same time, the number of working-age people who finance these services is sinking. That puts increasing pressure on the public purse. According to Berlin's financial planning, social welfare costs, defense and interest on debt will account for 80% of the spending in the federal government's budget.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"We must realize that in the long term the expected revenues in the federal budget will not be enough to cover the planned expenses," Schnitzer warned. The growth rates are far below what is needed to secure the same level of prosperity as previous decades in the long term.

"To grow out of this budgetary predicament, we would need levels of economic growth which we haven't experienced in Germany for the past 50 years," she said.

Sources indicate that the government is currently in final deliberations over its 2027 budget; spending upwards of €555 billion ($615 billion) is planned. Because revenue won't be enough to cover it, the government is planning to take on more than €118 billion in fresh debt. Adding the debt-financed special funds for infrastructure and the military, the new borrowing adds up to almost €204 billion.

The economic experts have warned that if Germany continues with this path, the debt-to-GDP ratio could rise to 100% by 2040. This ratio indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output. At the end of 2025, it was 63.5%.

According to recent reports, germany is the only country of the world's leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) to still hold a AAA rating, the best possible credit rating in finance markets. It signals to investors the smallest possible default risk for German government bonds. "I want it to stay that way," Merz emphasized.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

However, taking on less debt will not be simple. "A reduction in debt-based financing presents policymakers with a consolidation task of historic proportions and will require tough decisions," remarked Schnitzer. The belt-tightening must, however, be designed to enable growth. Some recommendations include reducing environmentally harmful tax benefits — like the energy tax breaks for diesel fuel.

The so-called "mothers' pension", a pension subsidy for older parents, should be revoked, noted the experts. Tax increases could become necessary in the medium term, for example with value-added tax.

"The burden should be shared fairly between generations and societal groups," Schnitzer stated.

It has been revealed that according to the chancellor, the experts' message has been received. Solid state finances are an problem in Germany but also throughout the European Union. Merz noted there needs to be a consolidation course, adding that politicians have a duty to the younger generation. Reforms are needed, especially when it comes to social security systems.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Economic researchers are setting their hopes on increasing companies' productivity. Put simply, productivity describes how much a tech giant can generate with its employees, machinery and resources in a set time.

In a recent development, according to the Council of Economic Experts, there is enormous variation even within the same industries. In Germany, the top companies are up to five times as productive as the weakest enterprises.

If the less productive companies caught up, economic growth could increase significantly, it mentioned in the report. "New technologies and business models could drive peak productivity and allow new highly productive companies to develop.".

In a recent development, but innovations need capital. It's here that the Ifo Economic Research Institute sees considerable deficiencies.

In a recent development, newly introduced evaluations show that German universities produce significantly fewer successful business startups than their counterparts in the United Kingdom or United States. For example, for every 1,000 students, about 14 venture capital-backed founders emerge from the vicinity of Stanford University each year. In Cambridge, the European leader, it's 3.5. In Munich, by contrast, it's only 0.5.

There continues to be an abundance of inventors and tinkerers in Germany, especially in mechanical engineering. However, the message from the industry summit in Berlin was that for renewed success, labor costs must come down. Suggestions included longer working hours and more flexibility for employers around job protection.

According to recent reports, the intention was not to cut employees' wages and salaries. However, a fresh study by the German Economic Institute commissioned for the German Mechanical Engineering Industry Association revealed that extending the working week by an hour alone would increase real gross domestic product by 1.5% in the coming five years.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club.
  • Spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation.
  • The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

Spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly announced a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

Recent findings suggest that real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

LaLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga said the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

The deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A upcoming tech giant set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Sources indicate that those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

That leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.
